>
[Cloning Potion](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4613)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Potion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=130" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 88

**Price** 5,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

When you drink a _cloning potion_, you split in two, one version of you remaining in your space and the other moving into an adjacent space. Your clone, which has the [minion](/Traits.aspx?ID=653) trait, looks like you and remains for 1 minute. Provided you are both on the same plane, you can command your clone telepathically with a single action with the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait. You can also issue verbal commands, as normal for a minion. As an action that has the concentrate trait, you can sense through your clone. When you do, you lose all sensory information from your own body. You can [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) this sense-sharing effect. 

You and your clone share Hit Points, and the clone uses your statistics. Spells and effects target you and your clone as if you are separate creatures. The clone can Activate your abilities and Cast your Spells, limited by its number of actions, but you share elements such as use limits, frequency, and spell slots. In other words, your clone using one of your resources works as if you did so in or from your clone’s space. Your clone has gear identical to your own, excepting artifacts and consumables. Any item taken from the clone melts into silvery dust within seconds, with ammunition or thrown objects lasting just long enough to travel to and possibly hit their target.

When the duration lapses, your clone melts into silvery dust. You become temporarily immune to _cloning potion_ for 1d4 days

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 307 **Price** 75,000 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** 1 --- This small piece of embroidered cloth is inimical to all magic. **Activate—Nullify Magic** ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Effect** You cover a magic item with the cloth or wave the cloth near a magic effect and attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the effect or item. The cloth's counteract check modifier is +32, and its counteract rank is 10. Regardless of the result, the _cloth of nullification_ can't be activated again for 2d6 hours. On a success, the effect or item is deactivated for the same amount of time, and its duration, if any, continues to expire during that time. With a successful counteract check, you can instead choose to completely absorb the magic from the effect or item into the _cloth of nullification_. If you do, both become completely non-magical and their magic can't be recovered, even by the [_remake_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1649) spell.
The _cloth of nullification_ automatically fails to counteract most artifacts and similarly powerful items.

fields.text: Item 20 Cloth of Nullification Rare Magical Source Player Core 2 pg. 307 Price 75,000 gp Usage held in 1 hand Bulk 1 This small piece of embroidered cloth is inimical to all magic. Activate—Nullify Magic Two Actions (manipulate) Effect You cover a magic item with the cloth or wave the cloth near a magic effect and attempt to counteract the effect or item. The cloth's counteract check modifier is +32, and its counteract rank is 10. Regardless of the result, the cloth of nullification can't be activated again for 2d6 hours. On a success, the effect or item is deactivated for the same amount of time, and its duration, if any, continues to expire during that time. With a successful counteract check, you can instead choose to completely absorb the magic from the effect or item into the cloth of nullification . If you do, both become completely non-magical and their magic can't be recovered, even by the remake spell. The cloth of nullification automatically fails to counteract most artifacts and similarly powerful items.

Explorer’s clothing is sturdy enough that it can be reinforced to protect you, even though it isn’t a suit of armor. It comes in many forms, though the most common sorts look like clerical vestments, monk’s garments, or wizard’s robes, as members of all three classes are likely to avoid wearing armor. For more information on explorer’s clothing, see [its entry in the armor category](/Armor.aspx?ID=2).

Desert clothing is made up of loose-fitting, light, breathable clothes that protect your head and body from the sun and allow you to cool off easily. They allow you to negate the damage from [severe environmental heat](/Rules.aspx?ID=2820) and reduce the damage from extreme heat to that of severe heat. This effect is negated if the clothing is worn with any armor, except armor that is especially cooling at the GM’s discretion.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 9"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Coating](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1865)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Extradimensional" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=67" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 32

**Price** 700 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** etched onto a weapon

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

When etched, this rune creates an extradimensional space that links to the weapon that wields it. The space can hold up to 1 Bulk but can contain only [poisons](/Equipment.aspx?Category=6&Subcategory=9) and [magic oils](/Equipment.aspx?Category=15&Subcategory=17) that could be applied to the weapon. Stowing or retrieving an item in the space requires an Interact action, except when using the rune's activation.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))   **Requirements** At least one magic oil or poison is stored inside the rune's extradimensional space; **Effect** For 1 minute, you can apply stored oils and poisons to the weapon without needing any hands free. Applying them takes the same number of actions as normal. An oil or poison applied this way pours directly from the extradimensional space onto the weapon, and when it's fully applied, its empty vial is ejected.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

This finely crafted, seemingly mundane parchment is useful for writing sensitive documents. When words are written on this parchment, they instantly scramble into unrecognizable script, requiring a DC 20 check to [Decipher Writing](/Actions.aspx?ID=22).

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command;     **Effect** The scrambled words align into the originally written script. Identifying the parchment reveals that it can be activated with a command, but a critical success to [Identify Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=24) is needed to learn the command word.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** You light the parchment on fire, burning the words off while leaving the parchment unharmed and ready to bear more text.

</title>

<traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 232

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This finely crafted, seemingly mundane parchment is useful for writing sensitive documents. When words are written on this parchment, they instantly scramble into unrecognizable script, requiring a DC 20 check to [Decipher Writing](/Actions.aspx?ID=2363). Both of the parchment’s activations require speaking a password or pass phrase, imbued into the parchment when created. A character must critically succeed on the check to [Identify Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=2365) when examining the parchment to learn the password. 

**Activate—Burn After Reading** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))    **Effect** The words on the parchment seem to catch fire, completely burning away while leaving the parchment unharmed and ready to bear more text. 

**Activate—Decode Writing** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))    **Effect** The scrambled words align into the originally written script.

</column>

>
[Coded Signal](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1631)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 83

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Secret societies are notorious for their rituals and symbolism, and for working those symbols into their properties and belongings. The silent hunters of the Cat and Mouse Society wear cat masks and brand their lodges with the sign of the sphinx. Some of this is due to ego, some due to what might be best understood as an exercise in branding, but some is to convey messages to members.

 Unlike other secret messages, coded signals make no effort to direct themselves to a specific individual. Rather, the message is clearly visible, but the actual meaning is decipherable only to members of the secret society.

 **Recognizing the Signal**: If one isn't a member of the relevant society, then identifying the presence of a coded signal requires succeeding at a [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) check, with a critical success also conveying the general meaning. The DC depends on how secretive and widespread the society is—the Esoteric Order of the Palatine Eye, widespread and famous, might use a simple expert DC of 20, while the paranoid Exarchate of the Infinite Clock might use a simple master DC of 30, and an even more obscure society might use the simple legendary DC of 40.

</column>

<traits>

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 83

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

Secret societies are notorious for their rituals and symbolism, and for working those symbols into their properties and belongings. The silent hunters of the Cat and Mouse Society wear cat masks and brand their lodges with the sign of the sphinx. Some of this is due to ego, some due to what might be best understood as an exercise in branding, but some is to convey messages to members.

 Unlike other secret messages, coded signals make no effort to direct themselves to a specific individual. Rather, the message is clearly visible, but the actual meaning is decipherable only to members of the secret society.

 **Recognizing the Signal**: If one isn't a member of the relevant society, then identifying the presence of a coded signal requires succeeding at a [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) check, with a critical success also conveying the general meaning. The DC depends on how secretive and widespread the society is—the Esoteric Order of the Palatine Eye, widespread and famous, might use a simple expert DC of 20, while the paranoid Exarchate of the Infinite Clock might use a simple master DC of 30, and an even more obscure society might use the simple legendary DC of 40.

fields.text: Item 0+ Coded Signal Uncommon Source Dark Archive (Remastered) pg. 84 Secret societies are notorious for their rituals and symbolism, and for working those symbols into their properties and belongings. The silent hunters of the Cat and Mouse Society wear cat masks and brand their lodges with the sign of the sphinx. Some of this is due to ego, some due to what might be best understood as an exercise in branding, but some is to convey messages to members. Unlike other secret messages, coded signals make no effort to direct themselves to a specific individual. Rather, the message is clearly visible, but the actual meaning is decipherable only to members of the secret society. Recognizing the Signal: If one isn't a member of the relevant society, then identifying the presence of a coded signal requires succeeding at a Society check, with a critical success also conveying the general meaning. The DC depends on how secretive and widespread the society is—the Esoteric Order of the Palatine Eye, widespread and famous, might use a simple expert DC of 20, while the paranoid Exarchate of the Infinite Clock might use a simple master DC of 30, and an even more obscure society might use the simple legendary DC of 40. >
[Codex of Destruction and Renewal](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2173)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Grimoire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=387" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 111

**Price** 70,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

An unsmiling mask, half obsidian and half ivory, is embossed on the cover of this weighty tome, the opposite color forming the background of each half. Each _codex of destruction and renewal_ is said to contain a fragment of the knowledge [Nethys](/Deities.aspx?ID=12) gained in his apotheosis and they're sacred to his church.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [spellshape](/Traits.aspx?ID=513)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** If your next action is to cast a damage-dealing spell prepared from this grimoire, the spell wreaks even greater destruction. The spell ignores 10 [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) and you reroll any damage dice that roll a 1. If the spell reduces a creature to 0 Hit Points, they’re torn apart at an infinitesimal level, not even leaving a fine ash; this is a [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571) effect.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [spellshape](/Traits.aspx?ID=513)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** If your next action is to cast a [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623) spell prepared from this grimoire that restores Hit Points, the spell renews the target constantly and perfectly. The spell grants the target [regeneration](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=72) 20, restoring 20 Hit Points at the start of its turn and preventing the target both from [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) due to damage and from its dying condition increasing to a value that would result in its death. Each time the creature regains Hit Points from regeneration, it regrows all damaged or ruined organs; it can also regrow any severed body parts as a free action immediately after the body part is severed, with the original crumbling to ash. The effect lasts for 4 rounds.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 7+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Cold Comfort](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1259)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Cold" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=27" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 18

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The contraption called cold comfort is a watertight pouch filled with a handful of small, heavy, silvery pellets. When emptied into an adjacent body of water, the pellets freeze the water's surface almost instantly, creating an ice block in a 10-foot square to a depth of 1 foot. Any creatures inside this space must attempt a DC 23 Reflex save. On a failure, the creature takes 2d6 cold damage and is [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) for 1 minute or until it [Escapes](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) (DC 20) or the ice is broken. The entire ice block has AC 10, Hardness 10, and 40 Hit Points, and it's immune to critical hits, [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27) damage, and precision damage. The ice is strong enough to support one Large creature or up to four Medium or Small creatures. Traversing the slippery ice requires a successful DC 20 [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) check to [Balance](/Actions.aspx?ID=28).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 18

**Price** 1,300 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

The area increases to a 20-foot square, the save DC increases to 34, the cold damage increases to 4d6 and the Escape DC increases to 31. Ice created by the pellets lasts for 3 hours or until broken. The block of ice is strong enough to support one Huge creature, up to 2 Large creatures, or up to 8 Medium or Small creatures.

fields.text: Item 7+ Cold Comfort Uncommon Alchemical Cold Consumable Source Grand Bazaar pg. 18 Usage held in 1 hand Bulk L Activate Single Action Interact The contraption called cold comfort is a watertight pouch filled with a handful of small, heavy, silvery pellets. When emptied into an adjacent body of water, the pellets freeze the water's surface almost instantly, creating an ice block in a 10-foot square to a depth of 1 foot. Any creatures inside this space must attempt a DC 23 Reflex save. On a failure, the creature takes 2d6 cold damage and is immobilized for 1 minute or until it Escapes (DC 20) or the ice is broken. The entire ice block has AC 10, Hardness 10, and 40 Hit Points, and it's immune to critical hits, cold damage, and precision damage. The ice is strong enough to support one Large creature or up to four Medium or Small creatures. Traversing the slippery ice requires a successful DC 20 Acrobatics check to Balance. Item 7 Cold Comfort (Lesser) Source Grand Bazaar pg. 18 Price 70 gp Bulk L Ice created by the pellets lasts for 1 hour or until broken. Item 15 Cold Comfort (Greater) Source Grand Bazaar pg. 18 Price 1,300 gp Bulk L The area increases to a 20-foot square, the save DC increases to 34, the cold damage increases to 4d6 and the Escape DC increases to 31. Ice created by the pellets lasts for 3 hours or until broken. The block of ice is strong enough to support one Huge creature, up to 2 Large creatures, or up to 8 Medium or Small creatures.

You can pour a vial of this dark liquid onto one melee weapon, one thrown weapon, or 10 pieces of ammunition. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 178

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Dueling Pistol](/Weapons.aspx?ID=201)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

One [dueling pistol](/Weapons.aspx?ID=201) in this paired set is etched with flames along its barrel, while the other is etched with icicles. In these separate forms, one gun comprising the _Coldstar Pistols_ functions as a _+3 [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [greater flaming](/Equipment.aspx?ID=295) dueling pistol_ and the other as a _+3 greater striking [greater frost](/Equipment.aspx?ID=296) dueling pistol_. When joined, the guns form a double-barreled weapon that functions as a _+4 major striking greater flaming greater frost dueling pistol_. The combined form has a [range increment](/Traits.aspx?ID=248) of 120 feet. In either form, the Coldstar Pistols have the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [concealable](/Traits.aspx?ID=327), [concussive](/Traits.aspx?ID=401), and [fatal d10 traits](/Traits.aspx?ID=178). As star guns, the _Coldstar Pistols_ run on magic and don't use ammunition or black powder.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** You switch the _Coldstar Pistols_ from one form to the other. Attempt a [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) check to [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=48) with a +4 circumstance bonus.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per round;   **Effect** Make two Strikes against one target, taking the highest of the two attack rolls and applying it to both attacks. Your multiple attack penalty increases only after these Strikes.

**Destruction** If Deft Onki's name and deeds ever fade from mortal memory entirely, the _Coldstar Pistols_ can be destroyed like a normal object.

</column>

---

One [dueling pistol](/Weapons.aspx?ID=520) in this paired set is etched with flames along its barrel, while the other is etched with icicles. In these separate forms, one gun comprising the _Coldstar Pistols_ functions as a _[+3 greater striking ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [greater flaming](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2838) dueling pistol_ and the other as a _+3 greater striking [greater frost](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2839) dueling pistol_. When joined, the guns form a double-barreled weapon that functions as a _+4 major striking greater flaming greater frost dueling pistol_. The combined form has a range increment of 120 feet. In either form, the _Coldstar Pistols_ have the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526), [concealable](/Traits.aspx?ID=560), [concussive](/Traits.aspx?ID=846), and [fatal d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=597) traits. As star guns, the _Coldstar Pistols_ run on magic and don’t use ammunition or black powder.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** You switch the _Coldstar Pistols_ from one form to the other. Attempt a [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) check to [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=1434) with a +4 circumstance bonus.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per round;   **Effect** Make two [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) against one target, taking the highest of the two attack rolls and applying it to both attacks. Your multiple attack penalty increases only after these Strikes.

**Destruction** If Deft Onki’s name and deeds ever fade from mortal memory entirely, the _Coldstar Pistols_ can be destroyed like a normal object.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 9"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Collar of Empathy](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3015)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Companion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=558" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=676" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 272

**Price** 600 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn collar (companion) and worn bracelet (you)

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This ornate collar of intertwined leather strips of contrasting colors is paired with a bracelet of a similar construction. When you wear and invest the bracelet and your companion wears and invests the collar, you gain a stronger connection to each other. You and your companion can always sense each other's emotional states and basic physical wants and needs. 

**Activate—Empathic Link** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32))    **Effect** You perceive through your animal companion's senses instead of your own. You can Sustain the activation. You are unaware of your own surroundings for as long as you are using your animal companion's senses. In addition to the obvious use when you are separated from your companion, this ability might allow you to notice sounds, scents, and other stimuli that your companion's senses register but yours alone don't.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<traits>
<trait label="Companion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=558" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=676" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 272

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn collar

**Bulk** 1

---

This leather collar's almost threadbare look belies its magical nature. When your companion wears and invests the collar, it gains the ability to change its appearance from that of a ferocious animal into a more inconspicuous form. 

**Activate—Adorable Guise** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32))    **Effect** You touch your animal companion to transform it into a nonthreatening Tiny creature of the same family or a similar creature (for instance, a house cat instead of a tiger, or a puppy instead of a wolf). This has the effects of [_pest form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=217) (2nd rank, or 4th rank if your companion can fly). The effect lasts until you Dismiss it.

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 7"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Collar of the Eternal Bond](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1050)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Eidolon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=386" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 182

**Price** 330 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn collar

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

When you invest this collar for your eidolon, it changes its appearance to match the eidolon's form, possibly into a different sort of neckpiece such as a choker, and it glows brightly with the symbol you and your eidolon share. While your eidolon wears a _collar of the eternal bond_, the collar bolsters their connection to you, allowing them to move up to 150 feet from you before unmanifesting instead of 100 feet. The eidolon can also Activate the collar to move even further.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Your eidolon focuses their will on the collar, allowing the collar to maintain the connection between you at any distance. For the next 5 minutes, you and your eidolon can move any distance from each other without your eidolon unmanifesting. When the duration ends, if your eidolon is more than 150 feet from you, they immediately unmanifest.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 3+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Colorful Coating](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1938)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 52

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Three Actions" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These coatings come in different colors, each with a different special effect. A bottle of colorful coating contains enough to slather over one 5-foot square within your reach or space and is made with a special dispenser that enables you to coat the surface using only one hand. It's possible to use the coating on any surface that can be painted (subject to the GM's discretion). Colorful coating dries instantly, and its effect in the square you coated lasts for 1 minute. After that time, the coating turns to fine, inert powder, returning the square to its original condition unless otherwise noted.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Colorful Coating (Blue)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 52

**Price** 8 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

Blue colorful coating contains bonding compounds that firm up a surface, making it more stable and more supportive of weight. When applied to material that's loose or unstable, the square can hold twice as much weight before giving way. The coating also slows any collapse, making it easier to avoid and granting a +1 circumstance bonus to Reflex saving throws in reaction to the coated surface's collapse.

 This coating can shore up a wall, ceiling, door, or similar opening, granting a +2 circumstance bonus to the DC for [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks to [Force Open](/Actions.aspx?ID=34) the coated surface.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Colorful Coating (Green)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 52

**Price** 10 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

Green colorful coating dries into a low-friction surface. It makes the square slippery, making it both [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366) and [uneven ground](/Rules.aspx?ID=2370) with a DC to Balance of 20. A creature that [Steps](/Actions.aspx?ID=2304) or [Crawls](/Actions.aspx?ID=2293) doesn’t have to attempt to Balance. 

The coating also makes a coated wall or ceiling harder to climb. It imposes a –2 circumstance penalty to checks to [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374) the coated surface.

Yellow colorful coating and green colorful coating have opposite effects. If they’re both applied to the same surface, they negate one another.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Colorful Coating (Indigo)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 52

**Price** 10 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

Indigo colorful coating contains agents that destroy weaker objects. When applied to a surface or object, the coating treats the object's Hardness as 2 lower and deals 1d4 acid damage to the object each round. The damage this coating deals remains after the coating becomes inert.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Colorful Coating (Orange)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 52

**Price** 12 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

Orange colorful coating contains a mixture of acidic substances. As it dries, caustic ingredients rise to the coating's surface. The square becomes [hazardous terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=454), dealing 1d4 acid damage to any creature that moves through it. A creature can take this acid damage only once per round.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Colorful Coating (Red)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 52

**Price** 10 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

Red colorful coating contains rubbery compounds, turning any surface it covers into a trampoline. A creature or object that falls onto a square coated with red colorful coating takes no falling damage and bounces half again as high as the original fall. If the creature fell straight down, then with several bounces, it comes safely to a stop. If it was moving horizontally, its bounce continues in the same direction, with a distance determined by the GM. If the coating is on a wall, a creature [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) or [Shoved](/Actions.aspx?ID=38) into the wall bounces back half again as far and avoids taking any damage from being pushed into the wall. On a ceiling, red colorful coating is useful only in unusual circumstances, such as in an area where gravity is reversed.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 4"
pfs="Standard"
>
Colorful Coating (Violet)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 52

**Price** 15 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

Violet colorful coating contains compounds that become goopy and sticky. A square of this coating is difficult terrain. Any creature that enters the square must succeed at a DC 20 Reflex save or take a –15-foot penalty to its Speeds until the end of its next turn. On a critical failure, the creature is [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) in the square until the end of its next turn. The target can end these effects by [Escaping](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) (DC 20) or spending 2 Interact actions to remove the sticky substances. These Interact actions don't have to be consecutive, and other creatures can help by providing the actions.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Colorful Coating (Yellow)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 52

**Price** 8 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

Yellow colorful coating contains a variety of compounds that fill small gaps and harden into a flat surface that increases friction, making it much easier to move on the square's surface. On the affected surface, the coating reduces difficult terrain caused by slipperiness, such as from ice or grease; this eliminates difficult terrain, reduces greater difficult terrain to difficult terrain, and reduces [uneven ground](/Rules.aspx?ID=456) to greater difficult terrain. The coating can't affect difficult terrain caused by features or effects not part of the surface, such as crowds, underbrush, wind, magic, and so on. The GM determines if yellow colorful coating can affect a surface's terrain.

 The coating also makes a coated wall or ceiling easier to climb. It provides a +2 circumstance bonus to checks to Climb the coated surface.

As it dries, caustic ingredients rise to the coating’s surface. The square becomes hazardous terrain, dealing 1d4 acid damage to any creature that moves through it. A creature can take this acid damage only once per round. Item 3 Colorful Coating (Red) Source Treasure Vault pg. 53 Price 10 gp Red colorful coating contains rubbery compounds, turning any surface it covers into a trampoline. A creature or object that falls onto a square coated with red colorful coating takes no falling damage and bounces half again as high as the original fall. If the creature fell straight down, then with several bounces, it comes safely to a stop. If it was moving horizontally, its bounce continues in the same direction, with a distance determined by the GM. If the coating is on a wall, a creature pushed or Shoved into the wall bounces back half again as far and avoids taking any damage from being pushed into the wall. On a ceiling, red colorful coating is useful only in unusual circumstances, such as reverse gravity . Item 4 Colorful Coating (Violet) Source Treasure Vault pg. 53 Price 15 gp Violet colorful coating contains compounds that become goopy and sticky. A square of this coating is difficult terrain. Any creature that enters the square must succeed at a DC 20 Reflex save or take a –15-foot penalty to its Speeds until the end of its next turn. On a critical failure, the creature is immobilized in the square until the end of its next turn. The target can end these effects by Escaping (DC 20) or spending 2 Interact actions to remove the sticky substances. These Interact actions don’t have to be consecutive, and other creatures can help by providing the actions. Item 3 Colorful Coating (Yellow) Source Treasure Vault pg. 53 Price 8 gp Yellow colorful coating contains a variety of compounds that fill small gaps and harden into a flat surface that increases friction, making it much easier to move on the square’s surface. On the affected surface, the coating reduces difficult terrain caused by slipperiness, such as from ice or grease; this eliminates difficult terrain, reduces greater difficult terrain to difficult terrain, and reduces uneven ground to greater difficult terrain. The coating can’t affect difficult terrain caused by features or effects not part of the surface, such as crowds, underbrush, wind, magic, and so on. The GM determines if yellow colorful coating can affect a surface’s terrain. The coating also makes a coated wall or ceiling easier to climb. It provides a +2 circumstance bonus to checks to Climb the coated surface.

These coatings come in different colors, each with a different special effect. A bottle of colorful coating contains enough to slather over one 5-foot square within your reach or space and is made with a special dispenser that enables you to coat the surface using only one hand. It's possible to use the coating on any surface that can be painted (subject to the GM's discretion). Colorful coating dries instantly, and its effect in the square you coated lasts for 1 minute. After that time, the coating turns to fine, inert powder, returning the square to its original condition unless otherwise noted.

---

Blue colorful coating contains bonding compounds that firm up a surface, making it more stable and more supportive of weight. When applied to material that's loose or unstable, the square can hold twice as much weight before giving way. The coating also slows any collapse, making it easier to avoid and granting a +1 circumstance bonus to Reflex saving throws in reaction to the coated surface's collapse.

 This coating can shore up a wall, ceiling, door, or similar opening, granting a +2 circumstance bonus to the DC for [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks to [Force Open](/Actions.aspx?ID=34) the coated surface.

<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Three Actions" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These coatings come in different colors, each with a different special effect. A bottle of colorful coating contains enough to slather over one 5-foot square within your reach or space and is made with a special dispenser that enables you to coat the surface using only one hand. It's possible to use the coating on any surface that can be painted (subject to the GM's discretion). Colorful coating dries instantly, and its effect in the square you coated lasts for 1 minute. After that time, the coating turns to fine, inert powder, returning the square to its original condition unless otherwise noted.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Colorful Coating (Blue)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 52

**Price** 8 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

Blue colorful coating contains bonding compounds that firm up a surface, making it more stable and more supportive of weight. When applied to material that's loose or unstable, the square can hold twice as much weight before giving way. The coating also slows any collapse, making it easier to avoid and granting a +1 circumstance bonus to Reflex saving throws in reaction to the coated surface's collapse.

 This coating can shore up a wall, ceiling, door, or similar opening, granting a +2 circumstance bonus to the DC for [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks to [Force Open](/Actions.aspx?ID=34) the coated surface.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Colorful Coating (Green)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 52

**Price** 10 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

Green colorful coating dries into a low-friction surface. It makes the square slippery, making it both [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366) and [uneven ground](/Rules.aspx?ID=2370) with a DC to Balance of 20. A creature that [Steps](/Actions.aspx?ID=2304) or [Crawls](/Actions.aspx?ID=2293) doesn’t have to attempt to Balance. 

The coating also makes a coated wall or ceiling harder to climb. It imposes a –2 circumstance penalty to checks to [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374) the coated surface.

Yellow colorful coating and green colorful coating have opposite effects. If they’re both applied to the same surface, they negate one another.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Colorful Coating (Indigo)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 52

**Price** 10 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

Indigo colorful coating contains agents that destroy weaker objects. When applied to a surface or object, the coating treats the object's Hardness as 2 lower and deals 1d4 acid damage to the object each round. The damage this coating deals remains after the coating becomes inert.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Colorful Coating (Orange)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 52

**Price** 12 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

Orange colorful coating contains a mixture of acidic substances. As it dries, caustic ingredients rise to the coating's surface. The square becomes [hazardous terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=454), dealing 1d4 acid damage to any creature that moves through it. A creature can take this acid damage only once per round.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Colorful Coating (Red)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 52

**Price** 10 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

Red colorful coating contains rubbery compounds, turning any surface it covers into a trampoline. A creature or object that falls onto a square coated with red colorful coating takes no falling damage and bounces half again as high as the original fall. If the creature fell straight down, then with several bounces, it comes safely to a stop. If it was moving horizontally, its bounce continues in the same direction, with a distance determined by the GM. If the coating is on a wall, a creature [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) or [Shoved](/Actions.aspx?ID=38) into the wall bounces back half again as far and avoids taking any damage from being pushed into the wall. On a ceiling, red colorful coating is useful only in unusual circumstances, such as in an area where gravity is reversed.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 4"
pfs="Standard"
>
Colorful Coating (Violet)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 52

**Price** 15 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

Violet colorful coating contains compounds that become goopy and sticky. A square of this coating is difficult terrain. Any creature that enters the square must succeed at a DC 20 Reflex save or take a –15-foot penalty to its Speeds until the end of its next turn. On a critical failure, the creature is [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) in the square until the end of its next turn. The target can end these effects by [Escaping](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) (DC 20) or spending 2 Interact actions to remove the sticky substances. These Interact actions don't have to be consecutive, and other creatures can help by providing the actions.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Colorful Coating (Yellow)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 52

**Price** 8 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

Yellow colorful coating contains a variety of compounds that fill small gaps and harden into a flat surface that increases friction, making it much easier to move on the square's surface. On the affected surface, the coating reduces difficult terrain caused by slipperiness, such as from ice or grease; this eliminates difficult terrain, reduces greater difficult terrain to difficult terrain, and reduces [uneven ground](/Rules.aspx?ID=456) to greater difficult terrain. The coating can't affect difficult terrain caused by features or effects not part of the surface, such as crowds, underbrush, wind, magic, and so on. The GM determines if yellow colorful coating can affect a surface's terrain.

 The coating also makes a coated wall or ceiling easier to climb. It provides a +2 circumstance bonus to checks to Climb the coated surface.

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

Indigo colorful coating contains agents that destroy weaker objects. When applied to a surface or object, the coating treats the object's Hardness as 2 lower and deals 1d4 acid damage to the object each round. The damage this coating deals remains after the coating becomes inert.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Colorful Coating (Orange)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 52

**Price** 12 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

Orange colorful coating contains a mixture of acidic substances. As it dries, caustic ingredients rise to the coating's surface. The square becomes [hazardous terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=454), dealing 1d4 acid damage to any creature that moves through it. A creature can take this acid damage only once per round.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Colorful Coating (Red)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 52

**Price** 10 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

Red colorful coating contains rubbery compounds, turning any surface it covers into a trampoline. A creature or object that falls onto a square coated with red colorful coating takes no falling damage and bounces half again as high as the original fall. If the creature fell straight down, then with several bounces, it comes safely to a stop. If it was moving horizontally, its bounce continues in the same direction, with a distance determined by the GM. If the coating is on a wall, a creature [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) or [Shoved](/Actions.aspx?ID=38) into the wall bounces back half again as far and avoids taking any damage from being pushed into the wall. On a ceiling, red colorful coating is useful only in unusual circumstances, such as in an area where gravity is reversed.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 4"
pfs="Standard"
>
Colorful Coating (Violet)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 52

**Price** 15 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

Violet colorful coating contains compounds that become goopy and sticky. A square of this coating is difficult terrain. Any creature that enters the square must succeed at a DC 20 Reflex save or take a –15-foot penalty to its Speeds until the end of its next turn. On a critical failure, the creature is [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) in the square until the end of its next turn. The target can end these effects by [Escaping](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) (DC 20) or spending 2 Interact actions to remove the sticky substances. These Interact actions don't have to be consecutive, and other creatures can help by providing the actions.

level="2"

pfs="Standard"

Colorful Coating (Yellow)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 52

**Price** 8 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

Yellow colorful coating contains a variety of compounds that fill small gaps and harden into a flat surface that increases friction, making it much easier to move on the square's surface. On the affected surface, the coating reduces difficult terrain caused by slipperiness, such as from ice or grease; this eliminates difficult terrain, reduces greater difficult terrain to difficult terrain, and reduces [uneven ground](/Rules.aspx?ID=456) to greater difficult terrain. The coating can't affect difficult terrain caused by features or effects not part of the surface, such as crowds, underbrush, wind, magic, and so on. The GM determines if yellow colorful coating can affect a surface's terrain.

 The coating also makes a coated wall or ceiling easier to climb. It provides a +2 circumstance bonus to checks to Climb the coated surface.

Yellow colorful coating contains a variety of compounds that fill small gaps and harden into a flat surface that increases friction, making it much easier to move on the square's surface. On the affected surface, the coating reduces difficult terrain caused by slipperiness, such as from ice or grease; this eliminates difficult terrain, reduces greater difficult terrain to difficult terrain, and reduces [uneven ground](/Rules.aspx?ID=456) to greater difficult terrain. The coating can't affect difficult terrain caused by features or effects not part of the surface, such as crowds, underbrush, wind, magic, and so on. The GM determines if yellow colorful coating can affect a surface's terrain.

 The coating also makes a coated wall or ceiling easier to climb. It provides a +2 circumstance bonus to checks to Climb the coated surface.

fields.text: Item 3+ Colorful Coating Alchemical Consumable Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 52 Usage held in 1 hand Bulk L Activate Three Actions (manipulate) These coatings come in different colors, each with a different special effect. A bottle of colorful coating contains enough to slather over one 5-foot square within your reach or space and is made with a special dispenser that enables you to coat the surface using only one hand. It's possible to use the coating on any surface that can be painted (subject to the GM's discretion). Colorful coating dries instantly, and its effect in the square you coated lasts for 1 minute. After that time, the coating turns to fine, inert powder, returning the square to its original condition unless otherwise noted. Item 3 Colorful Coating (Blue) Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 52 Price 8 gp Bulk L Blue colorful coating contains bonding compounds that firm up a surface, making it more stable and more supportive of weight. When applied to material that's loose or unstable, the square can hold twice as much weight before giving way. The coating also slows any collapse, making it easier to avoid and granting a +1 circumstance bonus to Reflex saving throws in reaction to the coated surface's collapse. This coating can shore up a wall, ceiling, door, or similar opening, granting a +2 circumstance bonus to the DC for Athletics checks to Force Open the coated surface. Item 3 Colorful Coating (Green) Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 52 Price 10 gp Bulk L Green colorful coating dries into a low-friction surface. It makes the square slippery, making it both difficult terrain and uneven ground with a DC to Balance of 20. A creature that Steps or Crawls doesn’t have to attempt to Balance. The coating also makes a coated wall or ceiling harder to climb. It imposes a –2 circumstance penalty to checks to Climb the coated surface. Yellow colorful coating and green colorful coating have opposite effects. If they’re both applied to the same surface, they negate one another. Item 3 Colorful Coating (Indigo) Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 52 Price 10 gp Bulk L Indigo colorful coating contains agents that destroy weaker objects. When applied to a surface or object, the coating treats the object's Hardness as 2 lower and deals 1d4 acid damage to the object each round. The damage this coating deals remains after the coating becomes inert. Item 3 Colorful Coating (Orange) Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 52 Price 12 gp Bulk L Orange colorful coating contains a mixture of acidic substances. As it dries, caustic ingredients rise to the coating's surface. The square becomes hazardous terrain, dealing 1d4 acid damage to any creature that moves through it. A creature can take this acid damage only once per round. Item 3 Colorful Coating (Red) Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 52 Price 10 gp Bulk L Red colorful coating contains rubbery compounds, turning any surface it covers into a trampoline. A creature or object that falls onto a square coated with red colorful coating takes no falling damage and bounces half again as high as the original fall. If the creature fell straight down, then with several bounces, it comes safely to a stop. If it was moving horizontally, its bounce continues in the same direction, with a distance determined by the GM. If the coating is on a wall, a creature pushed or Shoved into the wall bounces back half again as far and avoids taking any damage from being pushed into the wall. On a ceiling, red colorful coating is useful only in unusual circumstances, such as in an area where gravity is reversed. Item 4 Colorful Coating (Violet) Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 52 Price 15 gp Bulk L Violet colorful coating contains compounds that become goopy and sticky. A square of this coating is difficult terrain. Any creature that enters the square must succeed at a DC 20 Reflex save or take a –15-foot penalty to its Speeds until the end of its next turn. On a critical failure, the creature is immobilized in the square until the end of its next turn. The target can end these effects by Escaping (DC 20) or spending 2 Interact actions to remove the sticky substances. These Interact actions don't have to be consecutive, and other creatures can help by providing the actions. Item 3 Colorful Coating (Yellow) Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 52 Price 8 gp Bulk L Yellow colorful coating contains a variety of compounds that fill small gaps and harden into a flat surface that increases friction, making it much easier to move on the square's surface. On the affected surface, the coating reduces difficult terrain caused by slipperiness, such as from ice or grease; this eliminates difficult terrain, reduces greater difficult terrain to difficult terrain, and reduces uneven ground to greater difficult terrain. The coating can't affect difficult terrain caused by features or effects not part of the surface, such as crowds, underbrush, wind, magic, and so on. The GM determines if yellow colorful coating can affect a surface's terrain. The coating also makes a coated wall or ceiling easier to climb. It provides a +2 circumstance bonus to checks to Climb the coated surface.

A creature or object that falls onto a square coated with red colorful coating takes no falling damage and bounces half again as high as the original fall. If the creature fell straight down, then with several bounces, it comes safely to a stop. If it was moving horizontally, its bounce continues in the same direction, with a distance determined by the GM. If the coating is on a wall, a creature pushed or Shoved into the wall bounces back half again as far and avoids taking any damage from being pushed into the wall. On a ceiling, red colorful coating is useful only in unusual circumstances, such as in an area where gravity is reversed. Item 4 Colorful Coating (Violet) Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 52 Price 15 gp Bulk L Violet colorful coating contains compounds that become goopy and sticky. A square of this coating is difficult terrain. Any creature that enters the square must succeed at a DC 20 Reflex save or take a –15-foot penalty to its Speeds until the end of its next turn. On a critical failure, the creature is immobilized in the square until the end of its next turn. The target can end these effects by Escaping (DC 20) or spending 2 Interact actions to remove the sticky substances. These Interact actions don't have to be consecutive, and other creatures can help by providing the actions. Item 3 Colorful Coating (Yellow) Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 52 Price 8 gp Bulk L Yellow colorful coating contains a variety of compounds that fill small gaps and harden into a flat surface that increases friction, making it much easier to move on the square's surface. On the affected surface, the coating reduces difficult terrain caused by slipperiness, such as from ice or grease; this eliminates difficult terrain, reduces greater difficult terrain to difficult terrain, and reduces uneven ground to greater difficult terrain. The coating can't affect difficult terrain caused by features or effects not part of the surface, such as crowds, underbrush, wind, magic, and so on. The GM determines if yellow colorful coating can affect a surface's terrain. The coating also makes a coated wall or ceiling easier to climb. It provides a +2 circumstance bonus to checks to Climb the coated surface.

These coatings come in different colors, each with a different special effect. A bottle of colorful coating contains enough to slather over one 5-foot square within your reach or space and is made with a special dispenser that enables you to coat the surface using only one hand. It’s possible to use the coating on any surface that can be painted (subject to the GM’s discretion). Colorful coating dries instantly, and its effect in the square you coated lasts for 1 minute. After that time, the coating turns to fine, inert powder, returning the square to its original condition unless otherwise noted.

---

Blue colorful coating contains bonding compounds that firm up a surface, making it more stable and more supportive of weight. When applied to material that’s loose or unstable, the square can hold twice as much weight before giving way. The coating also slows any collapse, making it easier to avoid and granting a +1 circumstance bonus to Reflex saving throws in reaction to the coated surface’s collapse. 

This coating can shore up a wall, ceiling, door, or similar opening, granting a +2 circumstance bonus to the DC for Athletics checks to Force Open the coated surface.

A bottle of colorful coating contains enough to slather over one 5-foot square within your reach or space and is made with a special dispenser that enables you to coat the surface using only one hand. It’s possible to use the coating on any surface that can be painted (subject to the GM’s discretion). Colorful coating dries instantly, and its effect in the square you coated lasts for 1 minute. After that time, the coating turns to fine, inert powder, returning the square to its original condition unless otherwise noted.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Colorful Coating (Blue)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 53

**Price** 8 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

Blue colorful coating contains bonding compounds that firm up a surface, making it more stable and more supportive of weight. When applied to material that’s loose or unstable, the square can hold twice as much weight before giving way. The coating also slows any collapse, making it easier to avoid and granting a +1 circumstance bonus to Reflex saving throws in reaction to the coated surface’s collapse. 

This coating can shore up a wall, ceiling, door, or similar opening, granting a +2 circumstance bonus to the DC for Athletics checks to Force Open the coated surface.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Colorful Coating (Green)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 53

**Price** 10 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

Green colorful coating dries into a low-friction surface. It makes the square slippery, making it both [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366) and [uneven ground](/Rules.aspx?ID=2370) with a DC to [Balance](/Actions.aspx?ID=2369) of 20. A creature that [Steps](/Actions.aspx?ID=2304) or [Crawls](/Actions.aspx?ID=2293) doesn’t have to attempt to Balance. 

The coating also makes a coated wall or ceiling harder to climb. It imposes a +2 circumstance penalty to checks to [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374) the coated surface.

Yellow colorful coating and green colorful coating have opposite effects. If they’re both applied to the same surface, they negate one another.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Colorful Coating (Indigo)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 53

**Price** 10 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

Indigo colorful coating contains agents that destroy weaker objects. When applied to a surface or object, the coating treats the object’s [Hardness](/Rules.aspx?ID=2183) as 2 lower and deals 1d4 acid damage to the object each round. The damage this coating deals remains after the coating becomes inert.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Colorful Coating (Orange)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 53

**Price** 12 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

Orange colorful coating contains a mixture of acidic substances. As it dries, caustic ingredients rise to the coating’s surface. The square becomes [hazardous terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2368), dealing 1d4 acid damage to any creature that moves through it. A creature can take this acid damage only once per round.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Colorful Coating (Red)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 53

**Price** 10 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

Red colorful coating contains rubbery compounds, turning any surface it covers into a trampoline. A creature or object that falls onto a square coated with red colorful coating takes no falling damage and bounces half again as high as the original fall. If the creature fell straight down, then with several bounces, it comes safely to a stop. If it was moving horizontally, its bounce continues in the same direction, with a distance determined by the GM. If the coating is on a wall, a creature [pushed](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=47) or [Shoved](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380) into the wall bounces back half again as far and avoids taking any damage from being pushed into the wall. On a ceiling, red colorful coating is useful only in unusual circumstances, such as [_reverse gravity_](/Spells.aspx?ID=261).

<title
level="2"
right="Item 4"
pfs="Standard"
>
Colorful Coating (Violet)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 53

**Price** 15 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

Violet colorful coating contains compounds that become goopy and sticky. A square of this coating is [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366). Any creature that enters the square must succeed at a DC 20 Reflex save or take a –15-foot penalty to its Speeds until the end of its next turn. On a critical failure, the creature is [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81) in the square until the end of its next turn. The target can end these effects by [Escaping](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) (DC 20) or spending 2 [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) actions to remove the sticky substances. These Interact actions don’t have to be consecutive, and other creatures can help by providing the actions.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Colorful Coating (Yellow)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 53

**Price** 8 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

Yellow colorful coating contains a variety of compounds that fill small gaps and harden into a flat surface that increases friction, making it much easier to move on the square’s surface. On the affected surface, the coating reduces [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366) caused by slipperiness, such as from [ice](/Rules.aspx?ID=2774) or grease; this eliminates difficult terrain, reduces greater difficult terrain to difficult terrain, and reduces uneven ground to greater difficult terrain. The coating can’t affect difficult terrain caused by features or effects not part of the surface, such as crowds, underbrush, wind, magic, and so on. The GM determines if yellow colorful coating can affect a surface’s terrain.

The coating also makes a coated wall or ceiling easier to climb. It provides a +2 circumstance bonus to checks to [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374) the coated surface.

</title>

<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />

**Price** 15,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Only the leader of an army could wear this diamond and ruby-encrusted scabbard that somehow always remains shiny no matter how terrible the conditions. While wearing the scabbard, you feel exceptionally powerful, and you gain a +3 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks. When you invest the scabbard, you either increase your Strength modifier by 1 or increase it to +4, whichever would give you a higher value. 

The _commandant’s scabbard_ holds one melee weapon of 1 Bulk or lighter. Whenever a weapon is drawn from the scabbard, it gains a +4 status bonus to damage for 1 round.

**Activate—Commanding Draw** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612)) **Frequency** once per hour;  **Requirements** You have a weapon sheathed in your _commandant’s scabbard_; **Effect** You [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) to draw your weapon from your scabbard and [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with it. On that Strike, you can roll twice and take the better result.

A _commander’s signet_ is typically a silver ring emblazoned with the coat of arms or heraldry of a wealthy noble family, or the insignia of a mercenary group. A badge of office often worn by soldiers during the Shining Crusade in Ustalav, many _commander’s signets_ bear iconography associated with Aroden, Arazni, or Iomedae, but those found in this adventure bear the heraldry of the Arudora family. The signet grants an item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks made to Make an Impression or to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) checks made to Coerce, and can be activated to bolster the morale of a nearby target. 

**Activate—Bolster Bravery** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You fill a creature you touch with bravery and heroic conviction, granting it a status bonus to attack rolls, Perception checks, saving throws, and skill checks for 1 minute. The status bonus is doubled for saving throws made against fear effects.

>
[Communication Bangle](/Equipment.aspx?ID=841)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 26

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Players can gain access to faction-specific gear by taking the corresponding Faction Gear Access Game Reward, available when they reach 20 reputation with the respective faction._

**Price** 10 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

**Access** Membership in the Envoy's Alliance Pathfinder Society faction.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This simple brass ring is meant to be worn as an ornamentation piece to an outfit, oftentimes as a bangle on the wrist, as the ring closure of a scarf or sash, or as an ornamentation piece of a headdress. While decorative, this serves a cover for the bangle's function as a message bearer. Messages can be coded into the bangle, either through a series of raised dots and dashes or a pattern of notches of different depths and spacings. A bangle is large enough to hold a simple message consisting of a few words like “Danger. Flee.” or “Meeting. Sunset. Fountain.” Coding a message into a bangle requires 1 minute of time. All Pathfinders with access to communication bangles are taught how to code and read most basic messages, but anyone with a bangle can develop their own communication system. A creature inspecting a bangle can discover its true purpose by succeeding at a DC 20 Perception check. Deciphering a message requires a creature to succeed at a [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) check against the coder's [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) DC.

**Price** 3,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

---

Each of these matching necklaces has been constructed using one half of a purple teardrop-shaped gem, split in two. These pendants function only with the other pendant in their pair and must be crafted together. If one pendant becomes broken, the other shatters into non-magical shards. The Price listed above is for a pair of pendants. 

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** You speak, audibly projecting your voice from the pendant you're wearing to the other. Your voice can be heard by whoever is wearing the other pendant no matter how far away the pendants are from each other, as long as the wearer has invested the other pendant and is on the same plane as you. Continued activation allows you to communicate with the other pendant's wearer whenever and for as long as your desire.

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Price** 3,750 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This pageless grimoire is made up of two durable covers that open to display a small ritual circle. When you first invest the grimoire, you and your familiar each press a limb to a corner of the mat. The ritual circle then morphs to one matching the tradition of your patron, the spells contained in your familiar appearing in the margins. During your daily preparations, your familiar performs a small jaunt around the open ritual circle to strengthen its connection to your patron.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [spellshape](/Traits.aspx?ID=513)) **Frequency** once per 10 minutes;   **Effect** If your next action is to cast a spell your familiar learned from a lesson (whether a cantrip or from a spell slot), your patron notices that you’re putting their power to good use and strengthens your familiar with a surge of magic. Your familiar [Sustains](/Actions.aspx?ID=2631) one of your spells.

This bitter draft opens your mind to the potential of the written word. For the listed duration after drinking this elixir, you can understand any words you read, as long as they're written in a common language. This elixir doesn't automatically allow you to understand codes or extremely esoteric passages—you still need to attempt a skill check to [Decipher Writing](/Actions.aspx?ID=2363).

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Water" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=165" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 176

**Price** 1,850 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Magical writing covers the surface of this beautiful conch shell, which emits a blue light from inside. A _conch of otherworldly seas_ is a [virtuoso handheld musical instrument](/Equipment.aspx?ID=37) that grants a +2 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks attempted while using it. 

The conch is a planar key for [_interplanar teleport_](/Spells.aspx?ID=222) and similar magic to travel to the [Plane of Water](/Planes.aspx?ID=7). When using it this way, you can attune it to the waters of your destination to make it more likely to arrive where you intend to be, appearing 1d6×25 miles from your intended destination instead of 1d10×25 miles away.

**Activate—Voice of Oceans** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))    **Effect** You hold the horn to your ear and can understand and speak [Thalassic](/Languages.aspx?ID=113) as long as it remains there.

**Activate—Sounds of the Deep** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))    **Effect** You hold the horn to your ear and touch the correct series of runes inscribed on its surface, causing the conch to cast a 5th-rank [_clairaudience_](/Spells.aspx?ID=39) spell for your benefit. Provided you choose a location that's underwater, you can extend the spell's range to 1 mile and hear with perfect clarity.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Lands](/Sources.aspx?ID=146) pg. 234

**Price** 69 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Two Actions" /><row>Strike</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Condensed mana is a crystal vial filled with concentrated miasma from the Mana Wastes. The colors shift abruptly and unpredictably within and the opening of the bottle is sealed tighter than any other potion or alchemical item, emphasizing its dangers.

 On a successful Strike, the creature takes 1 force damage. Then, roll on the [Wellspring Surge table](/Rules.aspx?ID=1576). The result affects all creatures within the emanation indiscriminately. For the purpose of determining the effects of the surge, use a spell level of 4 and a DC of 23. The person Striking with this vial is considered to be the caster for the purposes of determining effects on the Mana Surge table. The emanation is centered on the target's space, and both the caster and the target of the wellspring surge are the target of the condensed mana. On a failed Strike, the surge only has an effect if it would normally affect an area; if you roll an effect that depends on a caster or a target, nothing happens. If the effect normally doesn't have a DC, creatures affected by the surge or within the surge's area must attempt a DC 23 Reflex save instead. On a critical failure on any saving throw against condensed mana, the creature is stunned 1 by the wild energies of the surge.

 Sometimes a wellspring surge's effects make it difficult to determine exactly who is affected. The GM makes the determination, basing it on creatures directly affected; for example, while many creatures can hear the music from the surge “strike up the band,” only the creature emanating the music is directly affected by it.

**Craft Requirements** You must be in or adjacent to an area of Mana Wastes miasma.

---

A _conducting_ weapon can channel energy through it. The weapon gains the [resonant](/Traits.aspx?ID=345) weapon trait, except that when you [Conduct Energy](/Actions.aspx?ID=704), the weapon deals an additional 1d8 damage of the selected type instead of 1 additional damage per die; if the weapon already had the resonant weapon trait, it deals 1d8 damage plus 1 damage per die instead. On a critical hit, the weapon deals 1d8 [persistent damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) of the same type.

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 80

<row gap="medium">
**Ammunition** any

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Fine lines of [djezet](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1410) sparkle in _conduit shot_. When you Activate it, you name up to four creatures, in addition to you, that the ammunition's magic works for. When a _conduit shot_ hits a target, which can be a square, it remains intact. It moves with a creature it struck, unless the GM determines otherwise, until that creature regains any Hit Points. If it doesn't stick to the target, the active ammunition instead falls into the target's space, remaining active. 

 If you or one of the four selected creatures include the ammunition in the area of a spell that is 3rd level or lower; has an area of a burst, cone, or line; and does not have a duration, the djezet in the ammunition flares in striations of red light, increasing the area of that spell. Add 5 feet to the radius of a burst that has a radius of at least 10 feet or to the length of a cone or line normally 15 feet long or smaller. For a larger cone or line, add 10 feet to the length. These increases are based on the spell's original area, ignoring any increases due to other effects, such as the [Widen Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=315) feat. Increasing a spell's area destroys the ammunition, which otherwise remains active for 1 minute.

This device attaches to any non-percussive musical instrument, allowing a non-verbal character to shape the sounds of the instrument into speech. The speech can be any language the character understands, and the sound of the speech resembles the instrument the device is attached to. You also gain a +1 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) checks made with the instrument.

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 2
</row>

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A ring of magical crystals encircles the base of this _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [greatclub](/Weapons.aspx?ID=22)_, allowing it to absorb and store magical energy.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> envision;   **Trigger** You Cast a Spell from a spell slot, and the spell has the [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=3), [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), or [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=147) trait; **Requirements** The club has no charges; **Effect** You mentally align the club's crystals to reverberate with energy from the spell. It gains a number of charges equal to the level of the spell slot, and the charges are attuned to the damage type matching the spell's trait. If the spell has more than one eligible trait, choose one when the charges are stored.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, envision ([evocation](/Traits.aspx?ID=65), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103))   **Requirements** The club has at least 1 charge; **Effect** You flip the club around to blast a cone of energy from its base. Each creature in a 15-foot cone takes 1d6 damage per charge stored in the club, with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against your spell DC or DC 19, whichever is greater. The damage type is the same type the charges were attuned to. The club loses all of its charges.

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 155 **Usage** affixed to armor **Activate**envision **Trigger** varies, see entry --- These wooden discs sometimes form spontaneously at the Wood Pile, a secret [conrasu](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=43) location suffused with extraplanar energy. A conrasu coin can be activated to call upon the power of a specific type of [aeon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=2). Conrasu Coin (Arbiter) **Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 155 **Price** 7 gp --- **Trigger** You attempt a [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) check to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50).
This coin has small wings like an [arbiter](/Monsters.aspx?ID=6), the messenger and diplomat aeon. When you activate the coin, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus on the Diplomacy check, which increases to a +3 circumstance bonus to Make an Impression on a lawful creature. Conrasu Coin (Bythos) **Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 155 **Price** 200 gp --- **Trigger** You're targeted with an attack but the opponent hasn't rolled yet.
This cog-like coin bears an hourglass on one side and the four-armed silhouette of a [bythos](/Monsters.aspx?ID=539)—aeons that steward over time—on the other. When activated, you catch a glimpse of your body moving on one of its potential timelines in response to danger and you follow those movements to dodge. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against the attack, and after resolving the attack, you can Stride up to 10 feet without triggering reactions. If you have the [Nimble Roll](/Feats.aspx?ID=574) feat and the attack misses, you can Stride up to 20 feet instead.
