The shape and exact flavor of these chocolate-covered cookies vary slightly based on who prepares them and the language they are imbued with when crafted. Although named for their use in obfuscating communications, Diarra finds them useful for quite the opposite reason.

 After eating one of these treats, you can speak and understand the chosen language for the next hour. If you have the [Read Lips](/Feats.aspx?ID=5204) or [Sign Language](/Feats.aspx?ID=5213) feat, you can use that language with those feats. A _conspirator's cookie_ grants you a +1 item bonus to Diplomacy checks to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) or [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=2393) in the chosen language and you can add your level even if untrained.

**Craft Requirements** You must know the chosen language

This weathered crook is often carried by chaplains of more primal deities. The carved wooden shaft bears the marks of fire damage and smells of campfire meals past. It counts as a wooden [religious symbol](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2745) for deities who grant the [nature](/Domains.aspx?ID=85) domain. While traveling in exploration mode, you and your allies within 120 feet count anyone’s travel Speed of 15 feet or lower as 25 feet.

**Activate—Season of Grit** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You brandish the constant crosier high in the air and wave it about. All allies within 60 feet who can see the crosier receive a +1 status bonus to Fortitude saves and resistance 5 to persistent damage for 1 minute.

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Contagion metabolizers seek out toxins in the bloodstream and attempt to purify them into humors the body processes naturally. When you drink this elixir, it attempts a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) check with the listed counteract modifier to remove the highest-level [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126) or [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46) afflicting you. This takes longer for a disease—the counteract check doesn't happen until 10 minutes after you drink the elixir. After drinking, you become temporarily immune to contagion metabolizers for 1 hour.

 If you're a [chirurgeon alchemist](/ResearchFields.aspx?ID=2) and have [powerful alchemy](/Classes.aspx?ID=1), you can substitute your statistics when you create a contagion metabolizer using [Quick Alchemy](/Feats.aspx?ID=667), if your stats are higher. This replaces the counteract rank with half your level rounded up and the counteract modifier with your class DC – 10.

[Containment Contraption](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1594)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Outlaws of Alkenstar</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #179: Cradle of Quartz](/Sources.aspx?ID=122) pg. 79

**Price** 500 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** 6
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Full Plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=13)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This heavy, mechanized brass suit is studded with pistons, gears, dials, and gauges and topped with a front-facing thick glass porthole. The suit is a suit of _+1 [full plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=13)_. While worn, it completely encloses you, providing protection against inhaled toxins—you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to all saving throws made against such effects. The suit isn't airtight, however, and doesn't protect against drowning if you're immersed in water or suffocation if you're placed in a vacuum—at least, not until you activate it.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The containment contraption fills with breathable air and filters exterior air or water to create more breathable air for you, as needed. This state persists for up to 1 hour, during which time you can breathe normally in environments where you normally couldn't. During this time, your circumstance bonus to saving throws against inhaled toxins increases to +2, and you also gain a +2 circumstance bonus to saves against [olfactory](/Traits.aspx?ID=246) effects. This effect ends immediately if the containment contraption becomes broken.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

This _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=31)_ has a mirror-like blade free of tarnish despite being millennia old. While wielding it, you gain a +2 item bonus to checks to [Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=75). If you're an expert with the skill or attack roll you're using to Aid and you critically succeed, you grant your ally a +3 circumstance bonus to the triggering check instead of a +2 bonus.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 2+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Cooperative Waffles](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1911)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Processed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=487" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 47

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="" /><row>10 minutes ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Flash-cooked on a [waffle iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1403) and drizzled with alchemical syrups and compound butter, cooperative waffles bolster the supportive spirit of those who share the batch. You can split the waffles with one other creature. After you both eat half of the waffles to Activate them, when one of you uses [Follow the Expert](/Actions.aspx?ID=514) to follow the other, the circumstance bonus granted is 1 higher. The waffles' bonus lasts 24 hours or until you next make your daily preparations, whichever comes first. You can only be linked to one creature in this way at a time; if either of you eats cooperative waffles again, the effect of your previous waffles ends.

</column>

</title>

**Access** You're from the Mordant Spire

<row gap="medium">

---

Made of petrified wood, this mask evokes the form of a coral reef. When you wear it, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks to [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=2381), and any armor you’re wearing gains the [aquadynamic](/Traits.aspx?ID=792) trait. 

**Activate—Cohabitate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=670)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** For 1 minute, your body becomes a mobile coral reef, letting much smaller creatures pass through or shelter in it. Creatures at least one size category smaller than you can share your space. Allies that share your space gain a +2 circumstance bonus to their AC, and you gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) 5 to any damage caused by a creature sharing the same space as you.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 8+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Cordelia's Construct Key](/Equipment.aspx?ID=884)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 123

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Worn on a necklace, this intricate key grants you greater facility with [constructs](/Traits.aspx?ID=35). The key alerts you to constructs lurking around you. Whether or not you are [Investigating](/Actions.aspx?ID=516), the GM automatically rolls [secret](/Traits.aspx?ID=142) [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) checks for you when you see a construct pretending to be a normal object, statue, or the like. Typically, this check is [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4), or an appropriate [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) skill. On a success, you recognize the presence of the construct and gain the usual benefits of Recall Knowledge.

 While you're wearing the key, if your attack reduces a construct to 0 Hit Points, instead of destroying it completely, you can send it into a dormant state, from which you can study its inner workings and possibly (at the GM's discretion) spend time and money to reprogram or repurpose it. Even if you don't subvert it, you can [Repair](/Actions.aspx?ID=42) a construct rendered dormant this way, allowing you to return tomb guardians to their vigil after you've battled them. Additionally, you can activate the key in two ways to call a construct to serve you.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, Interact;  **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You turn the key in the air and create a magic glyph. The key casts 3rd-level [_summon construct_](/Spells.aspx?ID=318).

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 1 minute (command, envision, Interact);  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You place the key on a Small object and turn it, creating a simple animated object for 1 hour. The animated object has the statistics of an [animated broom](/Monsters.aspx?ID=18) but has no bristles Strike and can't attack. It performs simple and broad menial tasks for you in exploration or downtime but is too slow to react to individual commands to assist you in a combat encounter.

A greater key allows you to fully comprehend and thus partially bypass a construct's resistances. You ignore the first 5 resistance a construct has against your damaging effects, whether martial or magical. Additionally, the key's first activation casts a 5th-level _summon construct_, and its second activation lasts 8 hours.

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />

This short golden crown bears a number of gems, each placed in the center of an engraving of a star. While wearing the crown, you are overcome with a nurturing instinct and understand the best ways to help others. You gain a +3 item bonus to [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9) checks.

 When you invest the crown, you either increase your Wisdom score by 2 or increase it to 18, whichever would give you a higher score.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** A living creature within 60 feet would die;  **Effect** You reach out to the creature with a lifeline. The triggering creature receives the effects of [_breath of life_](/Spells.aspx?ID=29), except they recover 7d8 Hit Points.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> command;  **Frequency** once per hour; **Trigger** An ally within 60 feet fails a non-[secret](/Traits.aspx?ID=142) check;  **Effect** You call out to your ally and offer a reassurance. When an activated _corpsecaller round_ hits a target, the struck creature is called to the grave. It takes 4d10 negative damage with a DC 25 Fortitude saving throw. **Critical Success** The foe is unaffected.
**Success** The foe takes half damage.
**Failure** The foe takes full damage and is [doomed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=9). If the foe dies within the next 24 hours, its corpse is tethered to the [Negative Energy Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=2), making it easier to raise as an [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160). Creatures using the [_create undead_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=10) ritual on the foe's corpse receive a +2 circumstance bonus to their primary and secondary skill checks for the ritual.
**Critical Failure** As failure, except the foe takes double damage and is doomed 2.

A _corpseward pendant_ is usually shaped like the skull of a humanoid or small animal.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You become [undetectable](/Conditions.aspx?ID=96) to undead creatures for 10 minutes. [Undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) can’t see, hear, or smell you, or detect you with sensory capabilities such as [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=82). A creature can attempt a DC 18 Will saving throw to ignore this effect. If an undead has reason to believe that undetected opponents are present, it can still attempt to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) or [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) you. If you attempt to use a [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509) spell to damage undead, touch or damage an undead creature, or attack any creature while warded in this manner, the pendant’s effects immediately end. An undead creature who observes you in this manner or one who succeeds at the Will save is immune to the _corpseward pendant_ for 24 hours.

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 190

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn garment

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Perception** +20; [precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=2406) vision 30 feet, [imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=2407) hearing 30 feet

**Communication** [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) ([Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=155), [Empyrean](/Languages.aspx?ID=115), four other languages)

**Skills** [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +21, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +19, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) +19

**Int** +2, **Wis** +5, **Cha** +4

**Will** +20 

</column>

---        

Devotees of benevolent faiths fear and loathe corruption cassocks, each of which is dedicated to an [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521) deity. When the garment chooses a target, such as when it senses a worshipper of a deity who isn’t unholy, it alters its form to match another deity’s iconography, appearing to be a devoted vestments for that deity. Once donned, the cassock tries to subtly sway its wearer to the worship of its deity. If the wearer begins to succumb, the _corruption cassock_ gradually reverts to its true appearance, replacing its false iconography as its wearer converts.

A _corruption cassock_ functions as a [_devoted vestments_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3077) for any wearer it chooses. Once you invest the cassock, it fuses to you. While you remain loyal to another deity, you believe the cassock grants you a +2 item bonus to [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) checks and a +1 item bonus to the divine skill of the deity to whom you believe the cassock is dedicated. It does neither. The GM secretly adjusts your checks with those skills, causing you to fail at religious tasks more often. If you have multiple equal or lower item bonuses to the affected skills, the cassock takes precedence, negating those bonuses. If you convert to following the cassock’s true unholy deity, however, these bonuses function normally for you.

If you attempt to Cast a Spell that has the [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) trait, the cassock can force you to attempt a DC 28 Will save. On a failure, you’re [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 for one minute (stupefied 2 on a critical failure). A _corruption cassock_ uses this ability to convince you that your deity has forsaken you.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can spend only to cast a  cleric domain spell for a domain belonging to the deity you believe the cassock is dedicated to. If you don't spend this Focus Point by the end of this turn, it's lost. However, when you use this activation, the _corruption cassock_ can instead cast a domain spell of the same rank from its deity. It does so only to confuse and dismay you, harming your faith.

</column>

>
[Counterfeit Item](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1632)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 83

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Many secret societies dabble in ancient lore and rare antiquities. If one were to ask what their greatest challenge is, instead of evading police attention or dealing with the occasional mystic curse, most members would say it's separating counterfeit goods from real ones. Almost anything can be counterfeited, and counterfeiting is a major criminal enterprise with its own tricks, techniques, and intricacies. Some counterfeiters specialize in the production of adulterated coinage, while others produce beautiful legal documents with forged signatures and stolen stamps. Another class of forger produces artwork in the style of some great master, while ancient relics can be churned out by the dozen in subterranean workshops.

 You can hire a counterfeiter to create low-grade, medium-grade, or high-grade counterfeit goods. In all cases, the goods can still act as mundane examples of their type (a counterfeit copy of the queen's [longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=31) is still a longsword), and if the original is enchanted, then the counterfeiter attempts to fake the appropriate magical auras. Counterfeit goods don't have any other magical powers, though—a counterfeit scroll can't be used to Cast a Spell, for example. A counterfeit good can't be cheaper than the base item. For example, the sword couldn't be cheaper than a longsword, nor the scroll cheaper than a piece of parchment.

 An item sold to a store goes through a rigorous vetting process that is extremely likely to detect a counterfeit, so a secret society member can't simply create counterfeits and then sell them at a profit. Counterfeits excel in situations where the item's hand-off is illicit or the item doesn't need to pass intense scrutiny from an appraiser. 

**Detecting Counterfeits**: Determining something is counterfeit requires inspecting the item and succeeding at a relevant skill check against the counterfeit's DC. Typically, this is [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4), but one might use [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) to detect a fake reliquary or [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9) to realize a potion is mere snake oil. Low-grade counterfeits typically have a [very easy DC of the item's level](/Rules.aspx?ID=552), medium-grade counterfeits typically have a standard DC of the item's level, and high-grade counterfeits typically have a hard DC of the item's level.

>
[Counterfeit Item](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4131)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=293) pg. 84

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Many secret societies dabble in ancient lore and rare antiquities. If one were to ask what their greatest challenge is, instead of evading police attention or dealing with the occasional mystic curse, most members would say it's separating counterfeit goods from real ones. Almost anything can be counterfeited, and counterfeiting is a major criminal enterprise with its own tricks, techniques, and intricacies. Some counterfeiters specialize in the production of adulterated coinage, while others produce beautiful legal documents with forged signatures and stolen stamps. Another class of forger produces artwork in the style of some great master, while ancient relics can be churned out by the dozen in subterranean workshops.

 You can hire a counterfeiter to create low-grade, medium-grade, or high-grade counterfeit goods. In all cases, the goods can still act as mundane examples of their type (a counterfeit copy of the queen's longsword is still a longsword), and if the original is enchanted, then the counterfeiter attempts to fake the appropriate magical auras. Counterfeit goods don't have any other magical powers, though—a counterfeit scroll can't be used to Cast a Spell, for example. A counterfeit good can't be cheaper than the base item. For example, the sword couldn't be cheaper than a longsword, nor the scroll cheaper than a piece of parchment.

 An item sold to a store goes through a rigorous vetting process that is extremely likely to detect a counterfeit, so a secret society member can't simply create counterfeits and then sell them at a profit. Counterfeits excel in situations where the item's hand-off is illicit or the item doesn't need to pass intense scrutiny from an appraiser.

 **Detecting Counterfeits:** Determining something is counterfeit requires inspecting the item and succeeding at a relevant skill check against the counterfeit's DC. Typically, this is [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37), but one might use [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) to detect a fake reliquary or [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42) to realize a potion is mere snake oil. Low-grade counterfeits typically have a [very easy](/Rules.aspx?ID=2630) [DC of the item's level](/Rules.aspx?ID=2629), medium-grade counterfeits typically have a standard DC of the item's level, and high-grade counterfeits typically have a hard DC of the item's level.

[Countering Charm](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3070)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 287

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This glittering charm is made of a gemstone flawed with a leaden inclusion. Spellcasters can cast spells into _countering charms_ that they've invested or that are invested by a willing creature. The spell's effect doesn't occur; the spell's power is instead stored within the charm, replacing any spell previously there. The charm can hold only spells cast from spell slots, not cantrips or focus spells. While the charm is invested, the creature who has invested it knows what spell is stored within and automatically identifies that spell when it's cast. 

**Activate—Counter** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))  **Trigger** You are targeted by or within the area of the spell stored within the charm; **Requirements** You have a free hand; **Effect** You present the charm and attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the triggering spell, using the rank of the spell stored in the charm and a counteract modifier of +20. This expends the spell held in the charm.

The spell's effect doesn't occur; the spell's power is instead stored within the charm, replacing any spell previously there. The charm can hold only spells cast from spell slots, not cantrips or focus spells. While the charm is invested, the creature who has invested it knows what spell is stored within and automatically identifies that spell when it's cast. Activate—Counter Reaction (manipulate) Trigger You are targeted by or within the area of the spell stored within the charm; Requirements You have a free hand; Effect You present the charm and attempt to counteract the triggering spell, using the rank of the spell stored in the charm and a counteract modifier of +20. This expends the spell held in the charm. Item 11 Countering Charm Source GM Core pg. 287 Price 1,200 gp Item 15 Countering Charm (Greater) Source GM Core pg. 287 Price 5,500 gp The charm’s counteract modifier is +25. Item 18 Countering Charm (Major) Source GM Core pg. 287 Price 20,000 gp The charm’s counteract modifier is +30.

This ornate cryptex, made of bronze or similar metals, spins slowly until activated. When used as a catalyst to cast an _[_imaginary lockbox_](/Spells.aspx?ID=2002)_ spell, the cryptex turns to generate a random release phrase before crumbling to dust and placing the magical lockbox in your mind. Items from the lockbox can be retrieved by anyone adjacent to you with whom you’ve shared the release phrase with.

[Covenant Tea](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3140)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Potion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=130" />
<trait label="Tea" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=738" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #197: Let the Leaves Fall](/Sources.aspx?ID=222) pg. 77

**Price** 10 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact or 10 minutes (concentrate, Interact)</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This green tea is often steeped in a pot with a dried persimmon. Traditionally, all participants in a complex discussion start their conversation with a tea ceremony involving _covenant tea_, with each member of the group enjoying the covenant of the shared beverage. Some have been known to use trickery and sleight of hand to ensure only those whose goals align with the tea preparer are served _covenant tea_, while others in the group are served non-magical (but still delicious) green tea, thus subtly tipping the balance in discussion toward those the tea server favors. This practice has resulted in some regions referring to covenant tea as “trickery tea.” Regardless of what you prefer to call the tea, when you drink it, you gain a +1 item bonus to Diplomacy checks and to your Perception DC for 10 minutes. 

---

 [Tea Ceremony](/Traits.aspx?ID=738) The duration increases to 1 hour.

    level="1"
    right="Item 17"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Cowl of Keys](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2528)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Stolen Fate</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Apex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=10" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #192: Worst of All Possible Worlds](/Sources.aspx?ID=203) pg. 70

**Price** 15,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn cloak

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This simple, tattered cloak is a faded green and features small, stylized keys sewn throughout its length. While wearing the cloak, you fade into the shadows and gain a +3 item bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks. When you invest the cloak, you either increase your Dexterity score by 2 or increase it to 18, whichever would give you a higher score.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** You brush your hand against the cloak and your fingers transform into picks, tension wrenches, skeleton keys, and any other tools, providing you with a full set of [thieves' tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=58). This transformation doesn't otherwise hamper the normal use of your fingers or hands. These tools never break when you critically fail your check to [Pick a Lock](/Actions.aspx?ID=70). You can Activate the cloak again to revert your fingers to normal.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You place your hand against a wall, floor, or ceiling. You create a magical doorway within the surface that a creature can move through, as if the door had always been there. The doorway can penetrate up to 10 feet of material; particularly thick material, such as heavy stone walls, can cause this effect to fail, expending its use for the day. You can use an Interact action on the door to remove it from the surface and return it to its previous shape.

The doorway can penetrate up to 10 feet of material; particularly thick material, such as heavy stone walls, can cause this effect to fail, expending its use for the day. You can use an Interact action on the door to remove it from the surface and return it to its previous shape.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Lozenge" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=484" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 47

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This tangy gum cracks and pops in your mouth as you chew it. While you're chewing crackling bubble gum, for up to 10 minutes, you have an item bonus to saving throws against auditory and sonic effects.

 **Secondary Effect** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=147)) **Effect** You blow a bubble with the gum until it pops, after which it becomes inert. The pop deals sonic damage to all creatures in a 15-foot cone with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save. A creature that fails its save is also bound with sticky gum, taking a –10-foot item penalty to its Speed for 1 minute. The creature can remove the gum with a total of 3 Interact actions. These actions don't have to be consecutive, and other creatures can provide the actions as well.

[Cradle Minder](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1673)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Travel Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=141) pg. 103

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) This animal can be purchased as a pet, but cannot be combat trained or contribute to combat in any way._

**Price** 50 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Sought after in Cheliax, the cradle minder resembles an [imp](/Monsters.aspx?ID=109). Despite rumors they were given as part of household pacts with [devils](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=30), these creatures were bred from fiendish [frog](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1680). Amphibious, they have leathery wings, frog-like eyes, and a forgiving temperament. They're ideal companions for children, as they tend to bond closely with one person and let out loud croaks when they become aware of danger. They require fiendish earthworms (unique feed) regularly, so ensuring you have a stable food supply is a necessity for ownership.

</row>

<row gap="medium">

---

This rugged metal eyepiece etched with square patterns is designed to be worn over a single eye. Twisting the lens reveals a faint three-dimensional outline of an item you plan to build or repair, with helpful labels on the component parts. You gain a +1 item bonus to Crafting checks. When you Repair an item, increase the Hit Points restored to 10 + 10 per proficiency rank on a success or 15 + 15 per proficiency rank on a critical success.

May contain spoilers from Crown of the Kobold King **Source** [Crown of the Kobold King](/Sources.aspx?ID=148) pg. 114 **Price** 700 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** 1 --- This iron cresset appears as a cage-like basket with a metal bowl fitted into its base—a bowl sized perfectly to hold the severed head of a Medium or Small humanoid. **Activate** Interact; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You open the cresset by detaching the top and folding it back on a hinge so that a decapitated head can be placed inside the bowl. Once the cage lid is folded back over the head and latched in place, and as long as the decapitated head has been dead for no longer than 10 minutes before being placed inside the cresset, the head is no longer subject to decay, and bugs and pests (such as maggots) are prevented from consuming the remains. This doesn't prevent the rest of the corpse or its soul from becoming [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160), nor does it prevent effects that restore life to the dead (but note that some spells, such as [_raise dead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=243), can't be used to restore life to a decapitated corpse in the first place). If the head is later removed from within the cresset, the head's delayed decay immediately catches up with it in a few seconds, rendering it useless for further use inside of a _cresset of grisly interrogation_. **Activate** 1 minute (command, Interact); **Frequency** three times per day; **Requirements** A severed head is within the _cresset of grisly interrogation_; **Effect** You pose a question to the head contained within the cresset, and it animates briefly to reply with a short answer over the course of a minute. The cresset empowers the severed head with the ability to reply even without breath, granting the head a semblance of life, calling upon the physical remains' latent memories rather than summoning back the deceased's spirit. The head must be forcefully commanded to answer with a [secret](/Traits.aspx?ID=142) [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) check— other attempts to query the head without attempting an Intimidation check for a result automatically fail. Once activated in this way, this activation of a _cresset of grisly interrogation_ can't be performed again for 1 hour. The head answers the question based on the result of the secret Intimidation check against the Will DC the creature had when it was alive or DC 25, whichever is higher. **Critical Success** The head answers the question truthfully, to the best of its ability.
**Success** The head answers the question truthfully, but the answer is brief, cryptic, or repetitive.
**Failure** The head's answer provides false information, attempting to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=47) to you with a +15 [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) modifier, or the creature's original Deception, whichever is higher.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the head gains a +4 circumstance bonus to its Deception check, and the next time you use this activation of the _cresset of grisly interrogation_ during the next 24 hours, the result of your Intimidation check is one degree of success worse than the result you rolled.

This _+2 greater striking [grievous](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2841) [sawtooth saber](/Weapons.aspx?ID=423)_ has a red hilt and a purple-black blade. Favored by Red Mantis assassins who enjoy using illusions to confound their targets, a crimson bluff constantly flickers and flashes, creating brief afterimages that can be quite distracting. If you use a crimson bluff as part of a gesture when you [Create a Diversion](/Actions.aspx?ID=2387), you gain a +2 item bonus to your Deception check. 

**Activate—Shimmer Step** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You cast [_blur_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1455) and then you Step or Stride. 

**Activate—Swap Places** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** An enemy would hit you with a melee Strike; **Requirements** You are under the effects of _blur_; **Effect** You swiftly dodge to the side as a momentary image of yourself manifests to distract the foe. The triggering Strike uses the outcome for one degree of success worse than the result of the attack roll. The duration of your _blur_ effect is reduced by 2 rounds.

These ominous swords are decorated with crimson lacquer and serve as perfect conduits for the Crimson Oath’s power. The first was granted to Clarethe Iomedar by a mysterious patron who many Reclaimers believe to be an emissary of [Ragathiel](/Deities.aspx?ID=126). A _crimson brand_ is a _+1 striking [wounding](/Equipment.aspx?ID=309) [bastard sword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=15)_. When the wielder uses the crimson brand to cast [_invoke the Crimson Oath_](/Spells.aspx?ID=556), they can generate a 60-foot line or a 30-foot cone instead of the normal 20-foot cone. Whenever the wielder would inflict [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) on an undead creature with the _crimson brand_, they can instead wreathe the creature in ruby energy, inflicting the same amount of persistent positive damage instead of persistent bleed damage.

[Fulcrum Lenses](/Equipment.aspx?ID=942)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #165: Eyes of Empty Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=81) pg. 75

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

_Fulcrum lenses_ are unique magical crystals that each contain a sliver of [Nhimbaloth's](/Deities.aspx?ID=163) essence. They belong to a larger set of lenses created to manipulate or even bind the Empty Death; most of the other lenses are long lost and likely destroyed. The Haruvex family came into possession of four of the lenses, and they knew that bringing them together focused Nhimbaloth's attention in unprecedented and dangerous ways. Belcorra brought all four lenses to the Abomination Vaults with her, intending to install them in Gauntlight for her ultimate revenge upon Absalom. She also created a special receptacle called the [_Fulcrum Lattice_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=943) to hold the lenses so that their power could be focused together. She realized the danger of keeping the _fulcrum lenses_ too close together until the right time and spread them out among loyal groups in the Abomination Vaults' lowest levels for safekeeping.

 Belcorra keeps only the most powerful lens, the _Ebon Fulcrum Lens_, with her—indeed, as a ghost, it's the only one she can carry. **Source** [Prey for Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=231) pg. 103

**Price** 15,000 gp

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

</column>

---

These tomes are sacred to the Red Mantis assassins, who use them to scribe their spells and record their violent deeds. The first of them were created in Rahadoum, but when the Oath Wars forced the worshippers of Achaekek to flee Rahadoum, many were identified by their _crimson tomes_, which were destroyed on the spot. Less than a dozen volumes survived, and the secret of creating them has been lost to history. Rumors persist of a first edition of this rare tome—an artifact version of the one presented here, but if these rumors are true, even the Red Mantis have lost track of such a treasure.

 Each _crimson tome_ is bound in fine red leather with gold filigree on the cover and golden edge gilding. When an [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629) spell is prepared from this grimoire, it becomes more difficult to purposefully disbelieve. Creatures that attempt to disbelieve an illusion spell prepared from a crimson tome must roll their check twice and take the worse result; this is a misfortune effect. This does not affect the saving throws of spells with the illusion trait that call for a saving throw to resolve effects other than disbelief, such as with [_dizzying colors_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1500) or [_vision of death_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1742).

**Activate—Crimson Focusing** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** You have fewer Focus Points than your maximum number of Focus Points; **Effect** You draw on the _crimson tome's_ energies and regain one Focus Point; the _crimson tome's_ leather binding turns black until your next daily preparations.

**Activate—Achaekek's Gift** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [spellshape](/Traits.aspx?ID=513))  **Trigger** You kill a creature with a spell prepared from the _crimson tome_;  **Effect** The _crimson tome_ infuses the slain creature's mortal remains and soul. If an effect attempts to restore the slain creature to life, the _crimson tome_ immediately attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) that effect (counteract modifier +27, counteract rank 8). If the restoring effect is counteracted, you immediately learn the name, nature, and location of the creature or effect that attempted to bring the dead body back to life. You can only impart Achaekek's Gift on one creature at a time. If you use this ability on another creature, the previous creature loses Achaekek's Gift.

The first of them were created in Rahadoum, but when the Oath Wars forced the worshippers of Achaekek to flee Rahadoum, many were identified by their crimson tomes , which were destroyed on the spot. Less than a dozen volumes survived, and the secret of creating them has been lost to history. Rumors persist of a first edition of this rare tome—an artifact version of the one presented here, but if these rumors are true, even the Red Mantis have lost track of such a treasure. Each crimson tome is bound in fine red leather with gold filigree on the cover and golden edge gilding. >
[Cave Worm Repellent](/Equipment.aspx?ID=655)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Extinction Curse</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #155: Lord of the Black Sands](/Sources.aspx?ID=33) pg. 75

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="" /><row>1 minute (Interact)</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Cave worm repellent is a highly noxious oil that can be applied to a creature or sprinkled in a circle around a 10-foot-radius area. In either case, after it is applied, it lasts for 24 hours or until it is scrubbed clean with 1 minute of work.

 When applied to a creature, the repellent causes [cave worms](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=21) of the indicated type to avoid attacking that creature in melee as long as they have something else nearby to attack. The repellent does not deter a cave worm from making ranged attacks against a coated target. If no creatures are within a cave worm's reach and it wants to approach and make a melee attack, it approaches and attacks a non-coated creature if it can without spending more actions to do so. 

If the coated creature is swallowed by the designated type of cave worm, the cave worm must succeed at a Fortitude save or involuntarily regurgitate the swallowed creature on the next round (a single action).

 When sprinkled around an area, cave worm repellent negates any chance of a random encounter with the particular type of cave worm in that area, as the creatures purposefully avoid the affected area.

 Other types of repellent that function similarly to this one might exist at the GM's discretion. Uncommon or rare creatures are typically much harder to repel, and repellent against them might necessitate harvesting ingredients from the creatures themselves (such as the creature's liver or a certain gland).

>
[Crooner's Cravat](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3632)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Curtain Call</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #204: Stage Fright](/Sources.aspx?ID=245) pg. 80

**Price** 3,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn necklace

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This long, silky neckcloth has the ability to be tied into a convincing semblance of an elegant evening scarf, a worker’s neck kerchief, an elaborate cravat, or any other neckwear. It also provides a boost to vocal performances, enhancing both projection and the emotive qualities of a performance. In its natural state, this item appears as a long, white silk scarf. A _crooner’s cravat_ grants a +1 item bonus to all [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) checks, but this increases to a +2 item bonus for Performance checks to sing.

**Activate—Adjust Cravat** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You make adjustments to the _crooner’s cravat_, transforming it into any type of stylish chosen neckwear; as you do so, you cast a 1st‑rank [_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1568) on yourself.

**Activate—Influential Croon** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=642)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You pour emotion into your vocal performance, projecting an empathetic bond that fascinates listeners. You cast [_enthrall_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1516) (DC 30 Will save). When you first activate Influential Croon, you can also cast [_subconscious suggestion_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1692) on one creature within 30 feet (DC 30 Will save).

</column>

<trait label="Tattoo" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=262" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 38

**Price** 360 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** tattoo

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A series of evenly spaced, unblinking tattooed eyes line your skin. When you enter an area that contains creatures within 60 feet that are unnoticed to you, the GM rolls a [secret](/Traits.aspx?ID=142) Perception check for you against the creatures' [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) DCs. On a success, the creature becomes [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39) by you, rather than [unnoticed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=41), and on a critical success, the creature becomes [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) to you. All creatures in the area are then temporarily immune to your _crown of insight_ for 24 hours. The _crown of insight_ doesn't help you find hidden items or traps, nor can it help you discern a creature hiding in plain sight, such as a [gargoyle](/Monsters.aspx?ID=210) pretending to be an inanimate statue. Additionally, since the effect occurs when you move to enter an area that contains creatures, it doesn't detect an unnoticed creature [Sneaking](/Actions.aspx?ID=63) up on you.

---

A trio of brilliant gems have been set into this elegant golden crown. You gain a +3 item bonus to checks to Recall Knowledge, regardless of the skill. When you invest the crown, you either increase your Intelligence modifier by 1 or increase it to +4, whichever would give you a higher value. This gives you additional trained skills and languages, as normal for increasing your Intelligence modifier. You must select skills and languages the first time you invest the crown, and whenever you invest the same crown of intellect, you get the same skills and languages you chose the first time. 

**Activate—Search Your Mind** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You gain the effects of [_hypercognition_](/Spells.aspx?ID=156).

>
[Crown of the Companion](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1086)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Strength of Thousands</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Healing" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=89" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Positive" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=128" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #170: Spoken on the Song Wind](/Sources.aspx?ID=97) pg. 75, [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 151

**Price** 250 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn crown

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Stories tell of a forgotten king who once loved his subjects so much he was willing to give his own life energy for them. Whether true or not, this majestic wooden crown bears elaborate carvings depicting that tale. It's ringed with images of the same kingly figure giving more and more of himself to a throng of needy subjects. While wearing it, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You bow to an ally within 30 feet, creating a magical bond between the two of you. You cast [_shield other_](/Spells.aspx?ID=281) targeting the ally. The link remains even if you move more than 30 feet away from them. At the end of the spell's duration, your ally recovers 4d8 Hit Points and you recover half of what they recover.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 9"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Crown of the Kobold King](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1727)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Crown of the Kobold King</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Crown of the Kobold King](/Sources.aspx?ID=148) pg. 114

**Price** 700 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn headwear

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Originally, this magical crown was to be known as the _Crown of Toil_—a magic item crafted by the dwarven priest named Gristogar. He intended for the crown to bolster his ability to rule and herald in a new era of a dwarven kingdom that followed the teachings of [Droskar](/Deities.aspx?ID=28). Yet Gristogar wasn't equal to his own ambitions, and before he could complete the _Crown of Toil_, his cult died out and he ended his own life. For centuries, the incomplete crown lay dormant, but over that time, fragments of Gristogar's soul infused it—not enough to transform it into a truly intelligent item, but enough to give it a rudimentary need and desire to be completed.

 When the Kobold King Merlokrep discovered the discarded crown and placed it upon his head, the crown at last had agency— if not in a hale and hearty dwarf, at least in the frame of a powerful and ambitious kobold. Just as the crown began influencing Merlokrep, so too did the Kobold King's personality influence the crown. Today, the device is known as the _Crown of the Kobold King_, and while it still urges the one who wears it to build a kingdom of endlessly toiling workers, it no longer does so in honor of Droskar. Instead, it seeks the rise of a brutal kobold kingdom.

 The crown appears as a golden band surrounded by iron spikes that glisten with fresh blood—the addition of a kobold skull to the top is largely decorative, but one the crown has grown to “enjoy.” Even in its incomplete state, a few rituals away from its true potential, the _Crown of the Kobold King_ is a potent item. Wearing the crown grants you a +2 item bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) checks and a +1 item bonus to saving throws against [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68) effects.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The crown infuses you with the glorious conviction that you're meant to rule, granting you a +1 status bonus to attack rolls, saving throws, and Charisma-based skill checks for 1 minute.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes (envision, Interact);  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You cast a [_nightmare_](/Spells.aspx?ID=208) spell.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

fields.markdown:
**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 288 **Usage** worn headwear --- An elegant accoutrement for a witch who has come into the higher echelons of power, a _crown of witchcraft_ typically looks like a garland of flowering twigs, a jeweled circlet, or a tall hat of fine fabric. You gain a +1 item bonus to Intimidation checks, and if you're a witch, you gain a +2 item bonus to your patron skill.
If you have a familiar, you can attach a small portion of the crown's material to your familiar, such as a strip of fabric from a hat tied around its tail or a sprig of natural material linked to its collar; the familiar doesn't need to invest the item itself. If you do this, your familiar gains the [tough pet](/Familiars.aspx?ID=37) ability as long as the crown is invested by you. **Activate—Defiant Hex** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** Gain 1 Focus Point, which you can spend only to cast a witch [hex](/Traits.aspx?ID=324) spell. If you don't spend this point by the end of this turn, it is lost. **Craft Requirements** You are a witch. Crown of Witchcraft **Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 288 **Price** 1,000 gp Crown of Witchcraft (Greater) **Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 288 **Price** 21,000 gp --- The bonus to Intimidation checks is +2 and the bonus to your patron skill is +3.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 13"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Crushing Bough Bracers](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3622)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Wardens of Wildwood</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #203 Shepherd of Decay](/Sources.aspx?ID=243) pg. 76

**Price** 2,500 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Carved from the heartwood of some impossibly large tree on the [Plane of Wood](/Planes.aspx?ID=25) or [First World](/Planes.aspx?ID=35), crushing bough bracers enable wearers to cling to and shape plant material with ease. The pine cone designs appear to open and bare their seeds when the bracers are in especially verdant areas. 

The bracers grant you a 20-foot [climb Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2349) while climbing [plants](/Traits.aspx?ID=668) or [fungi](/Traits.aspx?ID=614). Your [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) deal damage to fungus, plant, and wood creatures as though their [resistances](/Rules.aspx?ID=2893) were 5 lower (minimum 0). In addition, the bracers allow you to cast [_timber_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1412) as an innate [primal](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=4) cantrip. When you cast _timber_ on a plane with the wood [planar essence trait](/Rules.aspx?ID=3020) (or a supernaturally verdant area, at the GM’s discretion), you can modify the spell in one of the following two ways: increase the spell’s area to 20 feet, to 25 feet if your proficiency rank for spell attack modifier and spell DC is expert, or to 30 feet if your proficiency is legendary; or increase the cantrip’s damage die size to d6.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

    level="1"
    right="Item 5"
    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Crushing Coils](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2377)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 191

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Leather Armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=4)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Made from constrictor snakeskin, the strips of this _+1 [leather armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=4)_ wrap around you like an anaconda might wrap around its victim. The first time you roll a 1 on any attack roll or check after donning the armor, it fuses with you and constricts. It constricts anytime you roll a 1 on any attack roll or check thereafter. When the armor constricts, you're [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=33) for 1 round.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** The armor wraps around you, allowing you to don it by the time the activation finishes.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<trait label="Cold" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=27" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Gadget" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=405" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 68

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) All Pathfinder Society agents have access to all uncommon clockwork items and gadgets from Chapters 1 and 2 of this book_

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

**Access**  Due to the use of technology, all gadgets are uncommon or rare, though inventors and regions with access to inventors have access to uncommon gadgets.

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

When you Activate a cryomister, you can either place it in an adjacent square or toss it up to 20 feet away. Once you've done so, the metallic device instantly disperses a heavy mist, settling quickly on nearby flat surfaces and forming a sheet of ice. The cryomister creates a burst with a radius depending on the type, making the affected area difficult terrain for 1 minute; at the GM's discretion, however, this duration might be reduced in unusually hot conditions or increased in unusually cold ones. If an affected square takes fire damage, the difficult terrain is removed. Though not designed as a weapon, the cryomister's rapidly cooling mist deals cold [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=150) damage depending on the type to creatures in the area on activation. Creatures attempting to move through the affected area can attempt an [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) check with a DC depending on the type to ignore the difficult terrain and move at their normal Speed. Throwing the cryomister onto the surface of a liquid creates a floating piece of ice for the same duration, capable of supporting one or more creatures of the listed size.

When you Activate a cryomister, you can either place it in an adjacent square or toss it up to 20 feet away. Once you’ve done so, the metallic device instantly disperses a heavy mist, settling quickly on nearby flat surfaces and forming a sheet of ice. The cryomister creates a [burst](/Rules.aspx?ID=2385) with a radius depending on the type, making the affected area difficult terrain for 1 minute; , at the GM’s discretion, however, this duration might be reduced in unusually hot conditions or increased in unusually cold ones. If an affected square takes fire damage, the [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366) is removed. Though not designed as a weapon, the cryomister’s rapidly cooling mist deals cold splash damage depending on the type to creatures in the area on activation. Creatures attempting to move through the affected area can attempt an [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) check with a DC depending on the type to [ignore the difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2367) and move at their normal Speed. Throwing the cryomister onto the surface of a liquid creates a floating piece of ice for the same duration, capable of supporting one or more creatures of the listed size.

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 572 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L --- This polished crystal sphere enhances scrying magic. Any visual information received through a spell with the scrying trait that was cast by the _crystal ball_ appears within the sphere, and any auditory information sounds out from the surface of the sphere. When you cast a [_scrying_](/Spells.aspx?ID=268) spell by any other means while holding the sphere, you can relay any information you receive in the same way, allowing others to see or hear the target. The base version of a _crystal ball_ is a sphere of clear quartz, but other versions are made of different stones. **Activate** 1 minute (command, envision, Interact); **Frequency** once per hour; **Effect** The _crystal ball_ casts [_clairvoyance_](/Spells.aspx?ID=40) to your specifications.
**Activate** 10 minutes (command, envision, Interact); **Frequency** twice per day; **Effect** The _crystal ball_ casts a DC 33 _scrying_ spell to your specifications.

---

This _[+2 resilient ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2804) [raiment ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2791) [explorer’s clothing](/Armor.aspx?ID=39)_ is a longline vest made of a flexible, durable lattice of many fine crystals. A wide variety of these vests exist, and their colors depend on the type of crystal that forms the lattice. The crystals glow briefly when an enemy hits the wearer. 

**Activate—Crystal Exoskeleton** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The crystals on your vest grow and extend, becoming an architecturally sculpted exoskeleton that covers your form. You gain 20 [temporary Hit Points](/Rules.aspx?ID=2321) that last for 1 hour. The exoskeleton crumbles into dust when the temporary Hit Points are depleted or when the duration ends, and the crystals return to their original state.

Activate—Crystal Exoskeleton Two Actions (concentrate, manipulate) Frequency once per day; Effect The crystals on your vest grow and extend, becoming an architecturally sculpted exoskeleton that covers your form. You gain 20 temporary Hit Points that last for 1 hour. The exoskeleton crumbles into dust when the temporary Hit Points are depleted or when the duration ends, and the crystals return to their original state.

**Source** [Impossible Lands](/Sources.aspx?ID=146) pg. 304 **Price** 3,000 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand --- A _cube of force_ is an enchanted cube that measures an inch across. While made from any hard material, the sides of a _cube of force_ are decorated so that they can be distinguished by touch. **Activate** Interact; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You hold the cube aloft and depress one of its six faces for several seconds. The cube creates six walls around you, creating a cube 10 feet on each side centered on you (typically centered on the top of your space if you're a Medium creature). If a creature or object overlaps any of these walls, that face of the cube doesn't appear; this also means if you're Huge or larger, the activation has no effect, as your space is larger than the cube would be. The duration and effect of the six walls depends on which face of the cube you press when you Activate the cube, as seen on Table 5: Cube Effects (below). Pressing the sixth cube face with a simple Interact action Dismisses the effect; doing so isn't an activation and thus doesn't count against the cube's frequency. The walls have the AC, Hit Points, and Hardness of a [_wall of force_](/Spells.aspx?ID=363). ## Cube Effects
**Cube Face****Duration****Effect**
1 30 minutes The walls keep out gas and wind, attempting to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) such effects that cross the threshold with a +20 counteract modifier but allowing all other things through.

fields.text: Item 13 Cube of Force Rare Evocation Magical Source Impossible Lands pg. 304 Price 3,000 gp Usage held in 1 hand A cube of force is an enchanted cube that measures an inch across. While made from any hard material, the sides of a cube of force are decorated so that they can be distinguished by touch. Activate Two Actions Interact; Frequency once per day; Effect You hold the cube aloft and depress one of its six faces for several seconds. The cube creates six walls around you, creating a cube 10 feet on each side centered on you (typically centered on the top of your space if you're a Medium creature). If a creature or object overlaps any of these walls, that face of the cube doesn't appear; this also means if you're Huge or larger, the activation has no effect, as your space is larger than the cube would be. The duration and effect of the six walls depends on which face of the cube you press when you Activate the cube, as seen on Table 5: Cube Effects (below). Pressing the sixth cube face with a simple Interact action Dismisses the effect; doing so isn't an activation and thus doesn't count against the cube's frequency. The walls have the AC, Hit Points, and Hardness of a wall of force . ## Cube Effects Cube Face Duration Effect 1 30 minutes The walls keep out gas and wind, attempting to counteract such effects that cross the threshold with a +20 counteract modifier but allowing all other things through. 2 10 minutes The walls block nonliving matter from crossing; a nonliving creature must succeed at a DC 30 Will save to cross the threshold, wasting their move action on a failure, and unattended objects can't cross. Non-magical ranged attacks can't cross either and instead attack the wall. A living creature can bring attended objects across the walls without needing to attempt a saving throw. 3 10 minutes The walls block living matter from crossing; a living creature must succeed at a DC 30 Will save to cross the threshold, wasting their move action on a failure. 4 5 minutes The walls keep out magical effects that cross the threshold, attempting to counteract magical effects with a +20 counteract modifier, though they don't prevent a creature with magical items or effects from entering. 5 1 minute The walls block everything, with the effects of wall of force . 6 — The cube is Dismissed (this takes only an Interact action and isn't an activation).

    right="Item 19"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Cube of Recall](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2189)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 114

**Price** 40,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This small cube has smooth matte sides. One side is black, the opposite side is white, and the other four are various shades of gray. Each side can be attuned to a location and then teleport you back to that spot in the blink of an eye.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** Pick one side of the cube and set it face up. You attune the cube to the location you currently occupy. Each side can be attuned to only one location. Once you use this action to attune to a location, the side you pick loses any previously attuned location.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710))    **Effect** While speaking a word of command and bringing the location into your mind, you push the corresponding side of the cube. You teleport to the location attuned to the side you press, within 100 feet of the attuned location, as long as that location is on the same planet. If it's not, your activation produces no effect, but the attunement remains.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Seven Dooms for Sandpoint</spoilers>

<traits>

<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />

**Source** [Pathfinder #200: Seven Dooms for Sandpoint](/Sources.aspx?ID=229) pg. 181

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn cloak

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The fabric of a _cultist cowl_ is either raspy burlap, durable cotton, or fine silk, depending on the item's power (and thus the implied import of the worshipper who wears it). When a character who worships a single deity dons a cultist cowl, the cowl's colors change to match those sacred to that deity, and the deity's symbol or rune appears on the lower front of the cowl that hangs just over the chest. These colors and symbols remain until a different worshipper wears the cowl. While worn, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) checks. You also gain a +1 item bonus to all skill checks attempted to aid a ritual by being a secondary caster.

---

The fabric of a _cultist cowl_ is either raspy burlap, durable cotton, or fine silk, depending on the item's power (and thus the implied import of the worshipper who wears it). When a character who worships a single deity dons a cultist cowl, the cowl's colors change to match those sacred to that deity, and the deity's symbol or rune appears on the lower front of the cowl that hangs just over the chest. These colors and symbols remain until a different worshipper wears the cowl. While worn, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) checks. You also gain a +1 item bonus to all skill checks attempted to aid a ritual by being a secondary caster.

The weapon performs divination magic on the blood of your foes, granting you insight into their abilities and weaknesses.

>
[Curious Teardrop](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2612)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="No Alignment" url="/Rules.aspx?ID=95" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Intelligent" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=280" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Metal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=505" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 146

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Perception** +26; [precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411) vision 60 feet, [imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412) hearing 30 feet

**Communication** [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=37) ([Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Talican](/Languages.aspx?ID=112))

**Skills** [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +24, Alchemy [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +26, Metal Lore +26, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) +24

**Int** +6, **Wis** +2, **Cha** +4

**Will** +26 

</column>

---        

A _curious teardrop_, despite being a sphere of liquid metal, hangs like an earring on a golden finding. The intelligent droplet is a spirited chatterbox, always observing and taking mental notes; however, it's easily overwhelmed by new sights, which often reduce it to a sobbing mess. Occasionally, the _curious teardrop_ enters a stage of melancholy over the fragility of all matter, requiring immense reassurance to pull it out of its nihilism.

 The tear prefers not to talk about its past, though it claims to be an actual tear separated from its “parent.” Clerics of [Laudinmio](/Deities.aspx?ID=274) maintain that the elemental lord is the only being capable of shedding a perfect, sapient tear of metal.

**Activate—Request a Spell** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You ask for the _curious teardrop's_ assistance. It casts [_curse of lost time_](/Spells.aspx?ID=683), [_ferrous form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1369), or 7th-rank [_elemental form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=98) (metal elemental only), depending on your request.

**Activate—Reflect Emotions** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32))  **Trigger** You're targeted by an [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60) or [metal](/Traits.aspx?ID=505) effect;  **Effect** You receive a +4 status bonus to your saving throw against the triggering effect. Whether or not your save is successful, the teardrop attempts a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) check at +36 to immediately reflect a copy of the effect back at the originator, targeting it using the creature's own relevant statistics but controlling the effect as if the teardrop had cast it.

</column>

fields.text: Item 16 Curious Teardrop Rare No Alignment Divine Intelligent Invested Metal Source Rage of Elements pg. 146 Usage worn Perception +26; precise vision 60 feet, imprecise hearing 30 feet Communication telepathy (Common, Talican) Skills Diplomacy +24, Alchemy Lore +26, Metal Lore +26, Society +24 Int +6, Wis +2, Cha +4 Will +26 A curious teardrop , despite being a sphere of liquid metal, hangs like an earring on a golden finding. The intelligent droplet is a spirited chatterbox, always observing and taking mental notes; however, it's easily overwhelmed by new sights, which often reduce it to a sobbing mess. Occasionally, the curious teardrop enters a stage of melancholy over the fragility of all matter, requiring immense reassurance to pull it out of its nihilism. The tear prefers not to talk about its past, though it claims to be an actual tear separated from its “parent.” Clerics of Laudinmio maintain that the elemental lord is the only being capable of shedding a perfect, sapient tear of metal. Activate—Request a Spell Two Actions (concentrate, manipulate) Frequency once per day; Effect You ask for the curious teardrop's assistance. It casts curse of lost time , ferrous form , or 7th-rank elemental form (metal elemental only), depending on your request. Activate—Reflect Emotions Reaction (concentrate) Trigger You're targeted by an emotion or metal effect; Effect You receive a +4 status bonus to your saving throw against the triggering effect. Whether or not your save is successful, the teardrop attempts a counteract check at +36 to immediately reflect a copy of the effect back at the originator, targeting it using the creature's own relevant statistics but controlling the effect as if the teardrop had cast it.

---

Curled cure secretes a gel that gently warms the skin and stimulates healing. You can Activate the item as part of the same activity you use to Treat Wounds. If you successfully Treat Wounds, you can also reduce the value of one of the targets' [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3), [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13), or [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) conditions by 1. The target of your Treat Wounds is then temporarily immune to curled cure gel for 24 hours, whether or not your attempt to Treat Wounds was successful.

---

This [tower shield](/Shields.aspx?ID=4) (Hardness 14, HP 56, BT 28) is composed of interlocking hexagonal wooden tiles lined with metal. The tiles are painted a verdant green, and each is marked with a faded rune that protects against curses. While you have this shield raised, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against spells that target you, increasing to a +2 circumstance bonus against [curses](/Traits.aspx?ID=38). You can unleash the energy stored in the shield to destroy a curse before it can affect you.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> command;  **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You are targeted with a curse spell; **Requirements** The _cursebreak bulwark_ is raised; **Effect** You activate the shield's countermeasures. It casts 8th-level [_remove curse_](/Spells.aspx?ID=250) with a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) modifier of +27 against the triggering curse.

>
[Immaculate Instrument](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3514)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=537" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=579" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 203

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn or held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This object, made of silver light, takes the form of a small musical instrument, prop, or other tool associated with a specific art form. The holder of the _immaculate instrument_ never suffers from creative blocks of any kind and their work is always insightful and skilled. A character who uses the _immaculate instrument_ to [Perform](/Actions.aspx?ID=2401) or [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=2385) can attempt the check at mythic proficiency once per month, and as long as they possess their _immaculate instrument_, they treat any critical failures with these skills as failures.

**Destruction** If the holder uses the _immaculate instrument_ to intentionally produce a work that is not just mediocre or crass, but one that devalues the public opinion of the art form itself in a showing of at least 100 spectators, the instrument fades away in shame.

</column>

Cursed Immaculate Instrument
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=567" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 203

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

This _immaculate instrument_ has been cursed by the [sublime breath](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3408) it was taken from, causing it to warp, rust, or tarnish, though the holder of the instrument cannot perceive this and rationalizes away any attempt to explain the instrument's obviously cursed nature. Whenever the _cursed immaculate instrument_ is used to produce a work, the holder must succeed on a DC 16 flat check or the work fails, leaving the holder frustrated and raising the DC of subsequent flat checks by 1.

 When the DC reaches 20, the work fails as normal, but the holder continues to attempt it fruitlessly to the exclusion of all other activities, including eating, drinking, and sleep, until they expire or the curse is broken.

Runelord Xanderghul often crafted _Cyrusian wands_ to bolster his access to his favorite illusion spells. All _Cyrusian wands_ look different but equally audacious in their coloration, shape, and glittering gemstone adornments.

A _Cyrusian wand_ only ever contains an arcane spell with the illusion trait.

Spend 1 Mythic Point and reroll the flat check, then resolve the spell’s effects at mythic proficiency.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 4+"
    pfs=""
>
[Cyrusian Wand](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4045)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Revenge of the Runelords</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=11" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
<trait label="Wand" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=164" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 70

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Runelord Xanderghul often crafted _Cyrusian wands_ to bolster his access to his favorite illusion spells. All _Cyrusian wands_ look different but equally audacious in their coloration, shape, and glittering gemstone adornments.

A _Cyrusian wand_ only ever contains an arcane spell with the illusion trait. 

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;  **Frequency** once per day, plus overcharge;   **Effect** You Cast the Spell at the indicated rank. If you spend 1 Mythic Point as part of this activation, resolve the spell’s effects at mythic proficiency. 

**Activate—Presume Success** <actions string="Reaction" /> ;  **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You fail the DC 10 [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333) when you overcharge the wand;  **Effect** You disbelieve your failure, willing the check to success. Spend 1 Mythic Point and reroll the flat check, then resolve the spell’s effects at mythic proficiency.

**Craft Requirements** You must be a mythic arcane spellcaster capable of supplying a casting of the spell at the listed rank.

Runelord Xanderghul often crafted _Cyrusian wands_ to bolster his access to his favorite illusion spells. All _Cyrusian wands_ look different but equally audacious in their coloration, shape, and glittering gemstone adornments.

A _Cyrusian wand_ only ever contains an arcane spell with the illusion trait. 

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;  **Frequency** once per day, plus overcharge;   **Effect** You Cast the Spell at the indicated rank. If you spend 1 Mythic Point as part of this activation, resolve the spell’s effects at mythic proficiency. 

**Activate—Presume Success** <actions string="Reaction" /> ;  **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You fail the DC 10 [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333) when you overcharge the wand;  **Effect** You disbelieve your failure, willing the check to success. Spend 1 Mythic Point and reroll the flat check, then resolve the spell’s effects at mythic proficiency.

**Craft Requirements** You must be a mythic arcane spellcaster capable of supplying a casting of the spell at the listed rank.
