May contain spoilers from Wardens of Wildwood **Source** [Pathfinder #202: Severed at the Root](/Sources.aspx?ID=242) pg. 80 **Price** 5,800 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** 1 --- The _Cythbikian staff_ is a gnarled length of rotting wood, riddled with mold and fungal growths. Originally called the _Zibikian staff_ in honor of its creator, the green man [Zibik](/Deities.aspx?ID=685), with whom Ghorus communed before magically receiving this staff. Ghorus spent years using samples of the staff’s spores to invent weapons for his war against Taldor. When you invest this staff, a thin layer of fungi grows on your hands, remaining until your next daily preparations. If an enemy takes damage from any of the spells you cast by the _Cythbikian staff_, this fungus spreads up your arms, and you gain temporary Hit Points equal to double that spell’s level. These temporary Hit Points last 10 minutes. **Activate—Rule by Roots** ([fungus](/Traits.aspx?ID=614), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per week; **Effect** You plunge the _Cythbikian staff_ into the earth, causing a vast fungal network to spread out from the staff, coating the ground, plants, structures, and all creatures in a 100- foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) (DC 34 Reflex avoids) until the staff is removed or 24 hours have passed. Non-magical plants in the area die. A creature covered by these fungal growths is [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) and [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64), physically, by the fungus, as it moves them around like a living puppet. At the beginning of a grabbed creature’s turn, they can attempt to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) (DC 34). On a failure, the fungus forces them to spend all of their remaining actions moving toward and attacking the nearest creature in the area using melee [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) with any weapon at their disposal. The fungal growths pay no mind to how the bodies under their control operate, and grabbed creatures are twisted, bent, and contorted in ways that harm their body. Each round, at the end of a grabbed creature’s turn, they take 8d6 bludgeoning damage from this painful manipulation (DC 34 basic Fortitude save). A creature that successfully Escapes or is physically removed from the area is no longer grabbed or controlled. When the _Cythbikian staff_ is removed from the ground, or after 24 hours have passed, the mold dies and this effect ends. Over the course of a week, the mold decays and fertilizes the soil, providing valuable nutrients to the soil and preparing the region for new plant growth. **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Effect** You expend a number of charges from the staff to cast a spell from its list.
  • **Cantrip** [_ timber_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1412)
  • **1st**[_ wall of shrubs_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1414), [_wooden fists_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1417)
  • **2nd** [_ oaken resilience_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1617), [_splinter volley_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1410)
  • **3rd** [_ sudden blight_](/Spells.aspx?ID=2033), [_wall of thorns_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1752)
  • **4th** [_ murderous vine_](/Spells.aspx?ID=953), [_fungal infestation_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1993)
  • **5th** [_ life-draining roots_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1403), [_plant form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1637)
  • **6th** [_ lignify_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1404), [_tangling creepers_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1714)

This tiny serrated dagger looks like a miniature [sawtooth sabre](/Weapons.aspx?ID=65). Until activated, it is too small and ornamental to function as a weapon, which might allow it to be passed off as a weapon-shaped decoration.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** You transform the _dagger of eternal sleep_ into a _+1 [grievous](/Equipment.aspx?ID=298) striking dagger_ and Strike an unconscious target with the dagger. If you are not in an encounter or otherwise threatened and you roll a hit with your Strike, you get a critical hit instead. The damage from the Strike and the bleed from the critical specialization effect do not awaken the target, though the target becomes temporarily immune to this effect until the next time it wakes up, meaning further _daggers of eternal sleep_ awaken it as normal. The dagger disintegrates immediately after use.

>
[Dancing](/Equipment.aspx?ID=293)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 583

**Price** 2,700 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** etched onto a melee weapon

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A dancing weapon flies autonomously and strikes your foes.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, Interact;     **Effect** You Release the weapon and it dances through the air, fighting on its own against the last enemy you attacked, or the nearest enemy to it if your target has been defeated. At the end of your turn each round, the weapon can Fly up to its fly Speed of 40 feet, and then can either Fly again or Strike one creature within its reach.

 The weapon has a space of 5 feet, but it doesn’t block or impede enemies attempting to move though that space, nor does it benefit from or provide flanking. The weapon can’t move through an enemy’s space. The weapon can’t use reactions, and its Fly actions don’t trigger reactions.

 While it’s activated, a _dancing_ weapon makes Strikes with an attack modifier of +24 plus its item bonus to attack rolls. It uses the weapon’s normal damage but has a +0 Strength modifier. The weapon’s abilities that automatically trigger on a hit or critical hit still function, but the weapon can’t be activated or benefit from any of your abilities while dancing.

 Each round, when the weapon is finished using its actions, attempt a DC 6 flat check. On a failure, the activation ends and the weapon falls to the ground. You can’t activate the item again for 10 minutes.

</column>

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 288 **Usage** worn shoes **Bulk** L --- These brightly colored, soft-soled boots motivate you to perform risky stunts and grant you the agility to succeed. The boots grant you a +2 item bonus to Acrobatics checks and a +1 circumstance bonus to checks to Tumble Through an enemy's space.
The boots can grip solid surfaces and help you avoid a fall, allowing you to use the Grab an Edge reaction even if your hands aren't free. You treat falls as 10 feet shorter or, if you have the Cat Fall feat, treat your proficiency rank in Acrobatics as one degree better to determine the benefits of that feat. If you have Cat Fall and are already legendary in Acrobatics, you can choose the speed of your fall, from 60 feet per round up to normal falling speed. Daredevil Boots **Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 288, [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 609 **Price** 900 gp Daredevil Boots (Greater) **Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 288, [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 609 **Price** 14,000 gp --- The bonus to Acrobatics checks is +3, and the bonus to Tumble Through is +2. The boots can be activated. **Activate—Daredevil Impulse** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** The boots cast [_unfettered movement_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1732) on you.

---

These brightly colored, soft-soled boots motivate you to perform risky stunts and grant you the agility to succeed. The boots grant you a +2 item bonus to Acrobatics checks and a +1 circumstance bonus to checks to Tumble Through an enemy’s space.

 The boots can grip solid surfaces and help you avoid a fall, allowing you to use the Grab an Edge reaction even if your hands aren’t free. You treat falls as 10 feet shorter or, if you have the [Cat Fall](/Feats.aspx?ID=765) feat, treat your proficiency rank in Acrobatics as one degree better to determine the benefits of that feat. If you have Cat Fall and are already legendary in Acrobatics, you can choose the speed of your fall, from 60 feet per round up to normal falling speed.

Made from the smokebulbs that grow in Stonebreach, dark pepper is used as a common spice in dwarven cooking, but can also be an irritant in large quantities. Sacks of dark pepper are readily available in the Roundabout Market, but are less common in markets elsewhere in the city. You can toss a handful of dark pepper at an adjacent creature as an Interact action. The target must attempt a DC 16 Fortitude save to avoid coughing to the point of choking. On a failed save, the creature coughs uncontrollably, becoming [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) for 1 round. On a critical failure, the creature is instead flat-footed for 3 rounds.

You can toss a handful of dark pepper at an adjacent creature as an Interact action. The target must attempt a DC 16 Fortitude save to avoid coughing to the point of choking. On a failed save, the creature coughs uncontrollably, becoming flat-footed for 1 round. On a critical failure, the creature is instead flat-footed for 3 rounds.

[Darkvision Scope](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1212)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 180

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Characters with access to firearms gain access to accessories that can be used with those weapons._

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** attached to firearm or crossbow (scope)

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These scopes, popular with snipers and other sneaky sharpshooters who ply their trade in the dead of night, incorporate clouded crystals with magical properties into their design. While relatively useless under normal lighting conditions, these crystals can help bring things into focus when used in dim light. The scope is then given an enchantment to enhance these properties for use in darkness. The scope grants you a +1 item bonus to Perception checks involving sight in areas of dim light visible through the scope (as well as in areas of darkness, if the scope has been activated).

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** You gain [darkvision](/Rules.aspx?ID=415) until the beginning of your next turn, as long as you continue to look through the scope.

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 578 --- Darkwood is a very lightweight wood found primarily in old-growth forests in south-central Avistan; it is dark as ebony but has a slight purple tint. A darkwood item’s Bulk is reduced by 1 (or to light Bulk if its normal Bulk is 1, with no effect on an item that normally has light Bulk). The Price of an item made of darkwood is based on the item’s normal Bulk, not its reduced Bulk for being made of darkwood, but reduce the Bulk before making any further Bulk adjustments for the size of the item. ## Darkwood Items

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 578 --- Darkwood is a very lightweight wood found primarily in old-growth forests in south-central Avistan; it is dark as ebony but has a slight purple tint. A darkwood item’s Bulk is reduced by 1 (or to light Bulk if its normal Bulk is 1, with no effect on an item that normally has light Bulk). The Price of an item made of darkwood is based on the item’s normal Bulk, not its reduced Bulk for being made of darkwood, but reduce the Bulk before making any further Bulk adjustments for the size of the item. ## Darkwood Items

A darkwood item’s Bulk is reduced by 1 (or to light Bulk if its normal Bulk is 1, with no effect on an item that normally has light Bulk). The Price of an item made of darkwood is based on the item’s normal Bulk, not its reduced Bulk for being made of darkwood, but reduce the Bulk before making any further Bulk adjustments for the size of the item. ## Darkwood Items Darkwood Items Hardness HP BT Thin Items Standard-grade 5 20 10 High-grade 8 32 16 Items Standard-grade 7 28 14 High-grade 10 40 20 Structure Standard-grade 14 56 28 High-grade 20 80 40 Material Uses Darkwood Armor Darkwood Shield Darkwood Weapon Item 0 Darkwood Branch Source Core Rulebook pg. 578 Price 500 gp Bulk L Item 0 Darkwood Lumber Source Core Rulebook pg. 578 Price 5,000 gp Bulk 1 Item 8 Darkwood Object (Standard-Grade) Source Core Rulebook pg. 578 Price 350 gp (per Bulk) Item 16 Darkwood Object (High-Grade) Source Core Rulebook pg. 578 Price 6,000 gp (per Bulk)

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This shining symbol of [Sarenrae](/Deities.aspx?ID=16) depicts the goddess with her arms held wide. In the center of the symbol is a crystal reliquary with a perfect feather floating inside, glowing bright as a candle with the light of the goddess.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;  **Frequency** once per day for each spell;   **Effect** The dawnlight casts 1st-level [_disrupt undead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=79) or [_light_](/Spells.aspx?ID=171). The _dawnlight's_ spell attack roll and [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) modifier are +7, and any spell with the [light](/Traits.aspx?ID=100) trait is treated as though its counteract level were 1 higher for counteracting [darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=39).

**Craft Requirements** You have a spellcasting class feature with the [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) tradition.

</column>

---

Whenever you successfully counteract magical darkness while holding this symbol, the clash of magic unleashes a momentary flash of light. Creatures with [darkvision](/Rules.aspx?ID=415) in the area of the _light_ spell or targeted by it must succeed at a DC 23 Fortitude save or be [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) for 1 round. Those with [light blindness](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=22) are also exposed to [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407).

 Change the list of spells to 3rd-level versions of _disrupt undead_, _light_, and [_searing light_](/Spells.aspx?ID=269). The spell attack roll and counteract modifier are +13.

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 253 --- Dawnsilver is renowned for its lightness, durability, and effectiveness against a range of creatures including devils and werecreatures. It has the same sheen as silver but a slightly lighter hue. Dawnsilver weapons and armor are treated as if they were silver for the purpose of damaging creatures with weakness to silver. A metal item made of dawnsilver is lighter than one made of iron or steel: the item's Bulk is reduced by 1 (reduced to light Bulk if its normal Bulk is 1, with no effect on an item that normally has light Bulk). The Price of an item made of this material is based on the item's normal Bulk, not its reduced Bulk for being made of dawnsilver, but reduce the Bulk before making any further Bulk adjustments for the size of the item. ## Dawnsilver

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 253 --- Dawnsilver is renowned for its lightness, durability, and effectiveness against a range of creatures including devils and werecreatures. It has the same sheen as silver but a slightly lighter hue. Dawnsilver weapons and armor are treated as if they were silver for the purpose of damaging creatures with weakness to silver. A metal item made of dawnsilver is lighter than one made of iron or steel: the item's Bulk is reduced by 1 (reduced to light Bulk if its normal Bulk is 1, with no effect on an item that normally has light Bulk). The Price of an item made of this material is based on the item's normal Bulk, not its reduced Bulk for being made of dawnsilver, but reduce the Bulk before making any further Bulk adjustments for the size of the item. ## Dawnsilver

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Day Goggles](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1146)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 87

**Price** 30 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn eyepiece

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The darkened lenses of these goggles protect sensitive eyes from bright light but make seeing in the dark more difficult. While wearing day goggles, you gain a +1 item bonus to saving throws against [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163) [light](/Traits.aspx?ID=100) effects. However, while wearing the goggles, you take a –2 item penalty to visual Perception checks and you treat areas of bright light as dim light and areas of dim light as darkness for the purpose of whether you can see. While this is normally a disadvantage, if you have [light blindness](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=22), you aren't [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) in bright light as long as you continue wearing the day goggles, since to your eyes, there is only dim light. You can wear the goggles around your neck or on your forehead, granting no benefits, but allowing you to move them over your eyes with a single Interact action, without having to withdraw them first.

</column>

This glass bottle holds breezes captured from the heart of the Plane of Air. When you inhale the bottle’s contents, the air fills your lungs so completely that you no longer need to breathe, at least for a time. While the effect lasts, you also gain a status bonus against inhaled threats, such as inhaled poisons. This heavier-than-air mist emits a soft glow. While this poison lasts, it causes its victims to shine from within with agonizing, brilliant radiance. This effect has the [light](/Traits.aspx?ID=100) trait (although the poison itself doesn't, so only the light effect can be [counteracted](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) by [darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=39) effects). The [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34) condition from _daylight vapor_ can't be removed while the poison lasts, and when the victim enters an area of magical darkness, the poison attempts to counteract the darkness with a counteract modifier of +21. If the poison fails, it can't attempt to counteract the same darkness again. 

**Saving Throw** DC 31 Fortitude; **Onset** 1 round; **Maximum Duration** 6 rounds; **Stage 1** 4d6 poison damage and sickened 1 (1 round); **Stage 2** 6d6 poison damage and sickened 2 (1 round); **Stage 3** 10d6 damage and sickened 3 (1 round)

**Craft Requirements** Supply one casting of [_sunburst_](/Spells.aspx?ID=326).

May contain spoilers from Bastion of Blasphemies **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** 1 --- Each _Arudora memento_ is unique in appearance, but all seven are approximately the same size. Carried by each of the cursed family members, these mementos have within them the power to unlock entire portions of Bastardhall from the ghostly cursed state the castle traditionally exists in. Each of the seven mementos has the following activation, but the section of castle unlocked by each activation, as well as each memento’s specific benefit granted to the PCs, varies by type. **Activate—Return Memento** ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Effect** You place the memento into the appropriate statue’s clutches in the fountain located in area
**B3** of Bastardhall. The statue briefly animates to claim the memento, which turns to stone and becomes thereafter a permanent part of the statue, effectively destroying the memento while granting a boon to the party that persists for the remainder of this Adventure Path. A section of Bastardhall solidifies from its ghostly form, unlocking its reaches for the PCs to explore. **Destruction** An _Arudora memento_ is destroyed when it’s activated with Return Memento, and the boon it grants upon this returning lasts until the very end of the Adventure Path. Alisendra's Fan **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this elegant crimson hand fan is Returned, the dungeon (detailed in Chapter 5) is unlocked. The souls trapped in Bastardhall appreciate the end of Alisendra’s dominion and now whisper hints of truths in the ears of those who seek knowledge. The DCs for all checks made to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) are reduced by 1 for the rest of the Adventure Path. Augsten's Cudgel **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this bloodstained wooden cudgel is Returned, the reception halls (detailed in Chapter 4) are unlocked. Sometimes, violence is the only answer, and swift action to combat is rewarded. For the rest of the Adventure Path, all PCs gain a +1 bonus to any initiative rolls; this special bonus combines with all other bonuses. Dazerien's Thumbscrew **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this gory bronze thumbscrew is Returned, the private halls (detailed in Chapter 6) are unlocked. Rest becomes more rewarding now that the sadist of the dungeon has been defeated. For the rest of the Adventure Path, when the PCs take their 8-hour period of rest, they recover an additional number of Hit Points equal to their Constitution modifier (minimum 1) times their level. Irrokcis's Medallion **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this eerie medallion is Returned, the towers (detailed in Chapter 9) are unlocked, and the spirits of those trapped in Bastardhall rise up to aid the PCs. All weapon Strikes made by PCs deal an additional 1 spirit damage for the rest of the Adventure Path. Jinnivere's Riding Crop **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this leather riding crop is Returned, the cellars (detailed in Chapter 3) are unlocked. Companions are now more hearty and full of life—PC companions (such as familiars, eidolons, and animal companions) gain a +1 status bonus to all saving throws for the remainder of this Adventure Path. Raudltz's Telescope **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this handheld telescope is Returned, the fallen temple (detailed in Chapter 7) is unlocked. Secrets are now more difficult to hide in Bastardhall. Reduce all Perception DCs made when [Seeking](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) or [Searching](/Actions.aspx?ID=2630) by 2 for the rest of this Adventure Path. Ryhasphinea's Hourglass **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this cracked hourglass is Returned, the vaults (detailed in Chapter 8) are unlocked. Death’s grasp on the PCs wanes—for the rest of this Adventure Path, the DCs for all recovery checks made by a [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) PC are reduced by 2.

This _[+1 striking ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [shortbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=437)_ is a favorite of mage hunters and those who frequently fight enemies who can turn themselves [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=83). A creature who is critically hit with a ranged Strike from a dazzling shortbow must succeed at a DC 19 Fortitude save or be [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) for 1 minute.

**Activate—Show Yourself!** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You fire an arrow that glows with purple light at a spot. Each creature in a 10-foot burst within 60 feet is affected by [_revealing light_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1653) (DC 19).

**Craft Requirements** Supply one casting of _revealing light_.

---

_Deadlock mint_ is a species of mint with small, green flowers, said to grow on battlefields where the opposing sides were equally matched. Sprigs of the flowers blow gently in a breeze of their own creation. If you cast [_mystic armor_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1611) using _deadlock mint_, you release a small blast of concussive air in an [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) of a size that depends on the catalyst’s type. Unattended objects up to a certain Bulk limit are pushed away from you. Large or smaller creatures must succeed at a Fortitude save equal to your spell save DC or be pushed the same distance away from you.

---

_Deadlock mint_ is a species of mint with small, green flowers, said to grow on battlefields where the opposing sides were equally matched. Sprigs of the flowers blow gently in a breeze of their own creation. If you cast [_mystic armor_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1611) using _deadlock mint_, you release a small blast of concussive air in an [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) of a size that depends on the catalyst’s type. Unattended objects up to a certain Bulk limit are pushed away from you. Large or smaller creatures must succeed at a Fortitude save equal to your spell save DC or be pushed the same distance away from you.

Your joints loosen and bones thicken, making your body incredibly weighty and difficult to maneuver around. 

**Benefit** You gain an item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks to [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=38) and [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40), to your Fortitude and Reflex DCs against attempts to Shove or Trip you, and to saving throws against effects that attempt to force you to [move](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) or knock you [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31). 

**Drawback** You gain the [encumbered](/Conditions.aspx?ID=12) condition and can't remove it while under the effects of the mutagen.

When a creature enters the square, the magnets and ropes deploy, weighing down the creature's weapons and limbs. The creature must attempt a DC 18 Reflex save. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes a –1 status penalty to attack rolls for 1 round or until it [Escapes](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) (DC 18).
**Failure** The creature takes a –2 status penalty to attack rolls for 1 minute or until it Escapes (DC 18).
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the creature drops any metallic items it's holding.

>
[Deafening Music Box](/Equipment.aspx?ID=813)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Agents of Edgewatch</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=16" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #158: Sixty Feet Under](/Sources.aspx?ID=47) pg. 75

**Price** 500 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Symbols of musical notes decorate this gold-framed wooden cube measuring just under 1 foot by 1 foot. A funnel-shaped trumpet protrudes from the box's top at an angle, though it feels surprisingly light. The box has a large button on its side, and it must be set down on a flat surface in order to activate it; while it's activated, the rumbling and churning gears inside the box make it impossible to carry without dropping it.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** You press the button on the side of the music box, causing it to erupt with a cacophonous and discordant melody for 1 minute while it plays its entire melody, and it can't be shut off prematurely. The music is so loud that any creature within 60 feet must succeed at a DC 24 Fortitude save or become [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=8) for as long as they remain within 60 feet of the music box, and for 1 minute thereafter. On a critical success, a creature need not make any more saves and is temporarily immune to the _deafening music box_ for the next 24 hours; on a success, the creature must attempt a new save each round it remains within 60 feet of the music box.

</column>

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 79 **Price** 9,000 gp --- This modified Stasian coil of metal and glass stands about three feet tall. It activates when at least three creatures are within 20 feet of it, or if at least one creature stays within 20 feet of it for more than 1 round. It then lashes out with a torrent of electrical energy dealing 7d12 electricity damage to all creatures within 20 feet of it. Due to the fact that it doesn't trigger immediately when a creature enters its square, abilities like [Surprise Snare](/Feats.aspx?ID=2075) don't work with a death coil. Creatures within that area must attempt a DC 43 Fortitude saving throw. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes half damage.
**Failure** The creature takes full damage and is [stunned 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36).
**Critical Failure** The creature takes double damage is stunned 4.

Failure The creature takes full damage and is stunned 2. Critical Failure The creature takes double damage is stunned 4.

A weapon etched with a _deathdrinking_ rune shimmers with dark purple energy. When held by a living creature, the weapon causes twinges of hunger to manifest. 

While holding a _deathdrinking weapon_, you gain a +1 item bonus to saving throws against [negative](/Traits.aspx?ID=118) damage and [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=40) effects. When you critically hit a creature with a _deathdrinking weapon_, you inflict an additional 1d6 points of positive or negative damage to the creature— whichever type of damage would harm the creature. You also gain the following reaction when wielding a _deathdrinking weapon_.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** you kill or destroy a creature with the _deathdrinking weapon_;  **Effect** If the creature you killed was living, you gain a +1 item bonus to attack and damage rolls for 10 minutes. If the creature you destroyed was [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160), you gain a number of temporary HP equal to twice your level for 10 minutes.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Water" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=165" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 573

**Price** 320 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This item looks like an ordinary glass flask full of water. The stopper can’t be removed unless you speak one of the item’s three command words, each of which causes water to pour forth in a different way. Pulling the stopper straight out creates fresh water, and rotating it as you pull creates salt water. Any effect of the decanter lasts until the decanter is plugged (with its own stopper, a finger, or the like).

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command, Interact;     **Effect** Speaking “stream,” you cause water to pour out at a rate of 1 gallon per round.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command, Interact;     **Effect** Speaking “fountain,” you cause water to pour out in a 5-foot-long stream at a rate of 5 gallons per round.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command, Interact;     **Effect** Speaking “geyser,” you cause a powerful deluge of water to erupt at a rate of 15 gallons per round. You can direct the stream at a creature, subjecting it to the effects of [_hydraulic push_](/Spells.aspx?ID=154) (spell attack roll +15). You can repeat this once per round as long as the geyser continues, spending an Interact action to direct the geyser each time.

Activate Single Action command, Interact; Effect Speaking “stream,” you cause water to pour out at a rate of 1 gallon per round. Activate Single Action command, Interact; Effect Speaking “fountain,” you cause water to pour out in a 5-foot-long stream at a rate of 5 gallons per round. Activate Single Action command, Interact; Effect Speaking “geyser,” you cause a powerful deluge of water to erupt at a rate of 15 gallons per round. You can direct the stream at a creature, subjecting it to the effects of hydraulic push (spell attack roll +15). You can repeat this once per round as long as the geyser continues, spending an Interact action to direct the geyser each time.

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 182 **Price** 200 gp **Usage** held in 2 hands --- This set of 34 parchment cards usually comes in a velvet bag or simple leather wrap. Each card depicts a different creature, monster, or other being that, when the deck is activated, immediately appears as a believable, life-size illusion. You can look at the card's artwork, but no magical effect takes place until you Activate the deck, shuffling and drawing randomly. **Activate** envision, Interact; **Effect** You draw a card, chosen randomly from the remaining cards in the deck, and throw it to the ground to create an illusion of the creature depicted. The image is an [_illusory creature_](/Spells.aspx?ID=158), except it has a range of only 30 feet from where the card was thrown and the illusion lasts until destroyed or until anyone moves or damages the card. The creature takes its actions once on your turn if you're within 60 feet of the card and Sustain the Activation. The illusion ends if you don't Sustain it, or if you activate a new card from the deck. fields.markdown:
**Source** [Gamemastery Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=22) pg. 107 **Usage** held in 1 hand --- These 22 cards of heavy vellum, usually stored in a box or a pouch, bear images or glyphs depicting symbols of magical power. Looking at a card without activating it shows the card face but has no magical effect. Once the deck is face down, the cards randomize themselves—if you look at the top card multiple times, you may find it changes. Any card removed from the deck goes missing after a few seconds, reappearing in the deck. **Activate** envision, Interact; **Effect** You declare how many cards you will draw facedown from the deck, then draw your first card. The card takes effect immediately. Any further cards must be drawn within the next hour, and any card you don’t voluntarily draw flits off the deck and affects you anyway. You can never activate the same _deck of many things_ again. Once a card is drawn, it produces its effect immediately and then disappears back into the deck, which immediately shuffles itself. (The Dullard and Jester are exceptions, as described in their entries below.) The effects of each card are as follows.
  • **Balance** Your alignment changes to a radically different one. If you fail to adhere to that alignment, you lose a level and all the benefits you gained at that level. Your XP total doesn't change when you lose a level this way.
  • **Comet** If you alone defeat the next low-threat or harder hostile enemy or enemies you encounter, you gain enough XP to reach the next level. Otherwise, you gain no benefit.
  • **Donjon** You're imprisoned by a 10th-level [_imprisonment_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=13) ritual. This uses the prison option, typically sequestering you in a distant part of the world. You also lose all your items. Cease drawing cards.
  • **Dullard** Immediately reduce your Intelligence score by 1d4+1. You can then draw an additional card, and the Dullard card then disappears forever.
  • **Euryale** ([curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=38)) A [medusa's](/Monsters.aspx?ID=297) image curses you with a permanent –1 status penalty to all saving throws. This can be removed by only a deity or the Fates card.
  • **The Fates** The Fates respin the fabric of reality to save you from any situation you choose. This can reverse even a past event, and you can make the decision instantly even if the event would slay you. This intervention saves only you, not anyone else affected by the event. There's no limit on how long you can wait before using this effect.
  • **Flames** A fiend becomes filled with anger, jealousy, envy, or some other reason to despise you. Its hatred for you doesn't cease until either it or you is dead. It attacks you or otherwise attempts to foil you within 1d20 days. The GM determines the specifics of the fiend.
  • **Fool** You lose 1d10×100 XP unless you choose to draw two more cards.
  • **Gem** Gain your choice of 25 pieces of jewelry worth 200 gp each or 50 gems worth 100 gp each.
  • **Jester** You can either draw two more cards or gain 1d10×100 XP. The card then disappears forever.
  • **Key** Gain a magic weapon of 12th level or higher. The GM determines the item and what runes it has, if any.
  • **Knight** A [palace guard](/NPCs.aspx?ID=883) arrives and swears unfailing loyalty to you.
  • **Moon** Roll 1d4 to determine how many wishes the card grants you, which also affects the phase of the moon depicted on the card (1: crescent moon; 2: half moon; 3: gibbous moon; 4: full moon). These wishes each take one action to speak and have the effect of a [_wish_](/Spells.aspx?ID=377) spell.
  • **Rogue** One NPC ally becomes filled with hatred and immediately turns against you forever. The NPC might keep this hatred secret until an opportune moment.
  • **Ruin** You lose all your nonmagical possessions, including any wealth and property.
  • **Skull** You must immediately battle a [lesser death](/Monsters.aspx?ID=251). If slain in the battle, you can never be revived, except by a deity.
  • **Star** Gain an ability boost you must use immediately on one ability score of your choice.
  • **Sun** Gain 1,000 XP and a beneficial permanent magic item of 6th to 11th level, chosen by the GM.
  • **Talons** All your magic items disappear permanently, except for the deck and any artifact of higher level than the deck.
  • **Throne** You gain a permanent +4 status bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks, and you now own a small castle in any open area you wish. You must choose its location within 1 hour.
  • **Vizier** Upon request, you can learn the solution to any one problem or the correct answer to any one question, unless that information is obscured by a deity. This doesn't necessarily give you the means to act on that solution. You have 1 year to take the vizier's advice or lose its benefits.
  • **The Void** Your mind becomes trapped forever. This card is fickle, but it often throws the psyche into a prison in an object on a distant plane or planet. _Wish_ or similarly powerful magic can reveal your psyche's location, but it doesn't bring you back. Your comatose body continues to function. Cease drawing cards.
**Destruction** Trick the [Grim Reaper](/Monsters.aspx?ID=250) into drawing the Skull card.

fields.text: Item 22 Deck of Many Things Rare Artifact Magical Transmutation Source Gamemastery Guide pg. 107 Usage held in 1 hand These 22 cards of heavy vellum, usually stored in a box or a pouch, bear images or glyphs depicting symbols of magical power. Looking at a card without activating it shows the card face but has no magical effect. Once the deck is face down, the cards randomize themselves—if you look at the top card multiple times, you may find it changes. Any card removed from the deck goes missing after a few seconds, reappearing in the deck. Activate Single Action envision, Interact; Effect You declare how many cards you will draw facedown from the deck, then draw your first card. The card takes effect immediately. Any further cards must be drawn within the next hour, and any card you don’t voluntarily draw flits off the deck and affects you anyway. You can never activate the same deck of many things again. Once a card is drawn, it produces its effect immediately and then disappears back into the deck, which immediately shuffles itself. (The Dullard and Jester are exceptions, as described in their entries below.) The effects of each card are as follows. Balance Your alignment changes to a radically different one. If you fail to adhere to that alignment, you lose a level and all the benefits you gained at that level. Your XP total doesn't change when you lose a level this way. Comet If you alone defeat the next low-threat or harder hostile enemy or enemies you encounter, you gain enough XP to reach the next level. Otherwise, you gain no benefit. Donjon You're imprisoned by a 10th-level imprisonment ritual. This uses the prison option, typically sequestering you in a distant part of the world. You also lose all your items. Cease drawing cards. Dullard Immediately reduce your Intelligence score by 1d4+1. You can then draw an additional card, and the Dullard card then disappears forever. Euryale (curse) A medusa's image curses you with a permanent –1 status penalty to all saving throws. This can be removed by only a deity or the Fates card. The Fates The Fates respin the fabric of reality to save you from any situation you choose. This can reverse even a past event, and you can make the decision instantly even if the event would slay you. This intervention saves only you, not anyone else affected by the event. There's no limit on how long you can wait before using this effect. Flames A fiend becomes filled with anger, jealousy, envy, or some other reason to despise you. Its hatred for you doesn't cease until either it or you is dead. It attacks you or otherwise attempts to foil you within 1d20 days. The GM determines the specifics of the fiend. Fool You lose 1d10×100 XP unless you choose to draw two more cards. Gem Gain your choice of 25 pieces of jewelry worth 200 gp each or 50 gems worth 100 gp each. Jester You can either draw two more cards or gain 1d10×100 XP. The card then disappears forever. Key Gain a magic weapon of 12th level or higher. The GM determines the item and what runes it has, if any. Knight A palace guard arrives and swears unfailing loyalty to you. Moon Roll 1d4 to determine how many wishes the card grants you, which also affects the phase of the moon depicted on the card (1: crescent moon; 2: half moon; 3: gibbous moon; 4: full moon). These wishes each take one action to speak and have the effect of a wish spell. Rogue One NPC ally becomes filled with hatred and immediately turns against you forever. The NPC might keep this hatred secret until an opportune moment. Ruin You lose all your nonmagical possessions, including any wealth and property. Skull You must immediately battle a lesser death. If slain in the battle, you can never be revived, except by a deity. Star Gain an ability boost you must use immediately on one ability score of your choice. Sun Gain 1,000 XP and a beneficial permanent magic item of 6th to 11th level, chosen by the GM. Talons All your magic items disappear permanently, except for the deck and any artifact of higher level than the deck. Throne You gain a permanent +4 status bonus to Diplomacy checks, and you now own a small castle in any open area you wish. You must choose its location within 1 hour. Vizier Upon request, you can learn the solution to any one problem or the correct answer to any one question, unless that information is obscured by a deity. This doesn't necessarily give you the means to act on that solution. You have 1 year to take the vizier's advice or lose its benefits. The Void Your mind becomes trapped forever. This card is fickle, but it often throws the psyche into a prison in an object on a distant plane or planet. Wish or similarly powerful magic can reveal your psyche's location, but it doesn't bring you back. Your comatose body continues to function. Cease drawing cards. Destruction Trick the Grim Reaper into drawing the Skull card.

    level="1"
    right="Item 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Deck of Mischief](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1053)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Illusion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=92" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 183

**Price** 75 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This deck of 54 cards appears nearly identical to standard [playing cards](/Equipment.aspx?ID=873). Comprised of four thematic suits of 13 cards each, as well as two wildcards, the _deck of mischief_ is a favorite of scoundrels who prefer not to leave their games to chance—or to at least nudge the odds in their favor. If you know how to activate the deck, you can illusorily transform the ace and face cards into other cards in the deck.

 The deck is true to its name and less likely to comply with your wishes if not well cared for. While surprisingly resistant to the elements, a waterlogged, dirty, or battered deck may not function as desired, giving you incorrect information about which cards are still in the deck or failing to hold the illusion at a critical moment. If a deck becomes incomplete due to damaged or missing cards, it rapidly loses its deceptive capabilities and might even purposefully sabotage you.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision, Interact;     **Effect** You learn which of the ace and face cards are still in the deck. You can then swap the apparent face of an ace or face card in your hand (if you have any) with the face of one still in the deck. A creature who [Seeks](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) or touches the card can attempt to disbelieve this illusion (Perception DC 20).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Legends](/Sources.aspx?ID=40) pg. 28

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) For the purposes of Society play, the telepathic link created by a deepdread claw (page 28) ends when a Society adventure ends._

**Price** 4,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 or 2 hands

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Spear](/Weapons.aspx?ID=10)

---

One of a set of four identical spears collectively known as the Four Claws of the Deepdread, this weapon is fashioned from a single seamless piece of matte-black metal with a razored silver edge. In bright light, it functions as a _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [spear](/Weapons.aspx?ID=10)_, but in darkness or dim light, it becomes a _+2 greater striking spear_. You can upgrade its fundamental runes as normal for a specific weapon, starting from a _+2 greater striking spear_, but its fundamental runes are always one type worse in bright light.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command;     **Effect** You establish a telepathic link with someone else wielding a _deepdread claw_, enabling you to telepathically communicate with the creature while they possess the _deepdread claw_ regardless of distance, so long as you remain on the same plane. You can end a telepathic link you create or that you are part of as an action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, Interact;     **Effect** You cast 4th-level [_darkness_](/Spells.aspx?ID=59). You can see clearly in this darkness.

    right="Item 14"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Deflecting Branch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1448)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Strength of Thousands</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #172: Secrets of the Temple City](/Sources.aspx?ID=102) pg. 75

**Price** 4,500 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Greatclub](/Weapons.aspx?ID=22)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This massive branch has been cut into a general club shape but still bears several knots and has a number of runes carved along its length. The deflecting branch is a _+2 [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [greatclub](/Weapons.aspx?ID=22)_. On a critical hit, you knock the target [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31).

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per minute; **Trigger** You are the target of a physical ranged attack; **Requirements** You're aware of the attack and are not [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) against it; **Effect** You gain a +4 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack. If the attack misses, you have knocked it away. You can't use this ability to deflect unusually massive ranged projectiles (such as boulders or ballista bolts).

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per hour; **Trigger** You knock away a physical ranged attack by using the _deflecting branch's_ other activation;  **Effect** You swing the club and reflect the oncoming attack. The attack is redirected toward a creature within 60 feet. Make a ranged attack against the creature using your highest proficiency with a ranged weapon. 

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<row gap="medium">

---

A _demolishing_ weapon is made to destroy constructs. Damage inflicted on a construct with a _demolishing_ weapon continues to spread throughout the creature—cracks form, linkages fail, surfaces erode—and otherwise dismantle its body. When you damage a construct using a _demolishing_ weapon, you deal an extra 1d6 persistent force damage. On a critical hit, you deal an extra 1d12 persistent force damage instead.

</column>

---

A _demolition fulu_ allows a saboteur or excavator to be far away from the scene when demolition happens. The fulu crumbles to ash over 5 minutes to 8 hours, as you determine when you place the fulu. Once the duration ends, the fulu lowers the Hardness of the object it's affixed to by an amount equal to the fulu's level and then deals the listed damage to the object. A _demolition fulu_ serves as a hazard with a [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) DC to detect it and [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) DC to disable it according to its type.

    level="1"
    right="Item 13"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Demon Armor](/Equipment.aspx?ID=150)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Evil" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=64" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 557

**Price** 2,500 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** 4
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Full Plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=13)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Crafted from black iron, this crude suit of _+2 resilient [full plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=13)_ is designed to make you look like a horned demon, with your face peering out of the screaming maw of the beast.

While wearing the armor, you can attack with the helmet’s horns. They are a martial melee weapon with the effects of a _+2 weapon potency rune_. They deal 2d8 piercing damage and have the deadly d12 trait. On a critical hit with the horns, the target must attempt a DC 30 Fortitude save against the [_Abyssal plague_ disease](/Spells.aspx?ID=1). The horns can’t be etched with any runes. 

 If you aren’t evil, you’re drained 2 and can’t recover from this condition while wearing _demon armor_.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You cast [_dimension door_](/Spells.aspx?ID=69).

**Craft Requirements** You are evil; supply one casting of _dimension door_. 

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 15"
    pfs=""
>
[Demon's Knot](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2674)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Sky King's Tomb</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Evil" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=64" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #195: Heavy is the Crown](/Sources.aspx?ID=210) pg. 79

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn necklace

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The [demon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=28) Kaivirris is housed in the magnificent ruby that serves as the centerpiece of this beautiful, gold-plated, [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=272) pendant necklace. Creatures within 30 feet of the _demon's knot_ feel a subtle urge to acquire the necklace and take a –1 status penalty to Will saves.

 Upon donning the _demon's knot_, it fuses to you. You are subject to a [_geas_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=12) that requires you to free Kaivirris from his prison. If you die without completing this task, you become a [sulfur zombie](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1377) that always remains within 100 feet of the _demon's knot_ and is under the control of whoever is cursed by the _demon's knot_.

 The demon's knot sustains your physical form and protects your mind from mental control. You don't need to eat or drink. You become immune to the [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=5) and [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=6) conditions.

 The _demon's knot_ corrupts anyone wearing it. You gain weakness to cold iron 10 and good 10. Whenever you're within 60 feet of a [celestial](/Languages.aspx?ID=16), you're [frightened 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) and can't reduce the value of the frightened condition below 2.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You allow Kaivirris's corrupting influence over you to outwardly manifest. For 1 minute, your features adopt a cruel cast, and you radiate a palpable aura of evil. During this time, you gain a +2 status bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) checks, and your Strikes deal an additional 1d6 evil damage.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The demon's knot casts [_chilling darkness_](/Spells.aspx?ID=36).

**Destruction** A celestial creature must hold the necklace in their hands for at least an hour while meditating on the damage it has caused, then weep on the ruby. It must then be completely sealed within a cold iron container and cast into the heart of an active volcano, allowing the magma to melt the container and the necklace within.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Demon-Hunting Bands](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3540)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Convocation</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=564" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=579" />
<trait label="Holy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=517" />
<trait label="Talisman" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=709" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 66

**Price** 10 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** affixed to armor

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Free Action" /><row>([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))</row></row>

 

**Trigger** You Stride

 
</row>

</column>

---

These strips of supple leather, typically about 2 inches wide and 3 feet long, feature sigils, runes, and divine marks that reflect family lineage and beliefs in the old gods of Sarkoris. When activated, the band’s holy patterns surround you as you move, preventing your movement from triggering reactions from demons. The holy patterns scour nearby demons; any demons you pass adjacent to during the triggering movement take damage equal to their weakness to holy effects. You can activate the bands when you Burrow, Climb, Fly, or Swim (instead of Stride) if you have the corresponding movement type.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

This foul-smelling oil has the appearance and odor of the greasy, thick fluids that seep from a decaying body. When you spread this oil on an intact corpse that has been dead no longer than 1 week, its decay fades and the corpse is restored to the condition it was just after death. _Demortification oil_ can't undo damage done to a corpse after death, such as consumption by scavengers. Applied to a non-incorporeal undead, a dose of _demortification oil_ grants the undead creature a +1 item bonus to Armor Class for 1 hour.

>
[Deployable Cover](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1098)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 64

<row gap="medium">

**Hands** 2

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This thick mat of canvas, foliage, and wood is mounted on a tripod of flexible metal struts, folded into a baton- like shape, and clamped shut. You can rapidly deploy it on the ground with an Interact action to create cover. Deployable cover completely blocks one edge of the chosen square, allowing you (and others) to gain standard cover when you use the [Take Cover](/Actions.aspx?ID=2307) action. Before it can be used again, deployable cover must be carefully folded and clamped shut, which takes 1 minute.

Specially crafted to protect against bullet fire, a ballistic cover also works against other physical projectiles, such as arrows, bolts, and [thrown](/Traits.aspx?ID=195) weapons. While a creature has cover from Taking Cover behind a ballistic cover, it gains resistance 2 to piercing damage from ranged weapons and ranged [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attacks.

---

Carved with stylized images of water or aquatic life, _depth charges_ that are fired underwater or at a submerged target function with their normal range increments and can hit no matter their normal damage type. This ammunition explodes if it hits a target underwater, dealing bludgeoning damage in a 20-foot [burst](/Rules.aspx?ID=2385) ([basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude save) according to its type. This burst doesn’t extend out of the water.

This simple tool consists of a small iron weight attached to a thin rope that is marked at regular intervals (typically every foot). It can be used to measure the depth of a hole or body of water by dropping the weight down into unknown depths and counting the markings on the rope. It can also be used as a plumb bob.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 4"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Deravon's Helm](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5217)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Dead God's Hand</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=723" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [The Dead God's Hand](/Sources.aspx?ID=370) pg. 143

**Price** 90 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn headwear

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

_Deravon's helm_ is crafted with crown-like embellishments to give it an unmistakable air of authority. Crafted of gold with silver filigree incorporating images of swords, jewels, and most of all, the Eye of [Aroden](/Deities.aspx?ID=512) (from which the tines of the crown extend), _Deravon's helm_ is much lighter than would be expected. Downward swooping guards adorn the sides of the helm while leaving the face fully visible. It grants you a +1 item bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) checks made to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395).

**Activate—Bow Before Aroden** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=642), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You issue a command to a humanoid within 30 feet to bow down before [Aroden's](/Deities.aspx?ID=512) glory. The targeted creature must make a DC 18 Will save to resist being compelled to drop [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88) as its first action on their next turn (on a critical failure, the target must spend all three actions on its next turn remaining prone). If the target is a [human](/Traits.aspx?ID=627), they take a –1 status penalty to the save.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
[Destiny Blade](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5215)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Dead God's Hand</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [The Dead God's Hand](/Sources.aspx?ID=370) pg. 141

**Price** 60 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=386)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A _destiny blade_ 	is a _[+1](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2830) [throneglass](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5212) [longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=386)_ crafted to appear as a replica of [Aroden's](/Deities.aspx?ID=512) legendary sword, the _[Azlanti Diamond](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5220)_, affording lower-ranking knights in his service an opportunity to carry a bit of history with them in battle. On a critical hit with a _destiny blade_, the magic absorbs a portion of the target's luck and passes it on to the wielder, enhancing their destiny while hampering the victim. The target takes a –1 status penalty to saving throws and the wielder gains a +1 status bonus to saving throws. This lasts for 1 minute or until the wielder succeeds or critically succeeds at any saving throw, whichever comes first. This is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612) effect for the wielder and a [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=654) effect for the target struck.

---

Given to undisciplined acolytes at risk of breaking their vows, this fulu activates on its own if its wearer begins to perform an act anathema to a specific deity or cause, decided at the time of crafting. The fulu heats up when activated, giving you enough warning to correct your actions; if you proceed, the fulu immolates in a burst of flame. This deals 4d6 fire damage and brands your skin until you receive an appropriate _atone_ ritual. Either way, activating the fulu consumes it.

>
[Detector Stone](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1570)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Knights of Lastwall](/Sources.aspx?ID=123) pg. 90

**Price** 360 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

**Access** Knights of Lastwall have access to this item.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

During their journeys across the Gravelands, the Knights of Lastwall found several smoky, gemstone-like objects that knights refer to as _detector stones_. Some of the knights' Magaambyan allies believe the stones are [_aeon stones_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=407) corrupted by the same energies that corrupted the Gravelands, though they don't display the characteristic orbiting behavior of _aeon stones_ when invested. Despite the controversy, many knights use the stones for their ability to detect the presence of [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160).

 While you have a _detector stone_ invested, it glows faintly when an undead creature is within 30 feet of you, unless the undead is hidden or disguised with a [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) or [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) result of 20 or higher. An invested stone may be carried in a pocket, but some knights set them in necklaces, bracelets, or weapon hilts.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** You channel your life-force into the stone, empowering it temporarily. The stone can detect undead within 60 feet of you, rather than 30 feet, until the end of your turn. Undead hiding or disguising themselves must make an additional Deception or Stealth check to remain disguised or hidden from the activation, and the DC of the check is 23 rather than 20.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** one per hour;   **Effect** You focus on the stone as it glows, and your eyes glow with the same tainted light. You detect the auras of evil undead in a 30-foot radius around you and learn each aura's location and strength. This has the effects of a 2nd-level [_detect alignment_](/Spells.aspx?ID=65) spell but only detects evil undead.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

fields.text: Item 7 Detector Stone Uncommon Divination Invested Magical Source Knights of Lastwall pg. 90 Price 360 gp Usage worn Access Knights of Lastwall have access to this item. During their journeys across the Gravelands, the Knights of Lastwall found several smoky, gemstone-like objects that knights refer to as detector stones . Some of the knights' Magaambyan allies believe the stones are aeon stones corrupted by the same energies that corrupted the Gravelands, though they don't display the characteristic orbiting behavior of aeon stones when invested. Despite the controversy, many knights use the stones for their ability to detect the presence of undead. While you have a detector stone invested, it glows faintly when an undead creature is within 30 feet of you, unless the undead is hidden or disguised with a Deception or Stealth result of 20 or higher. An invested stone may be carried in a pocket, but some knights set them in necklaces, bracelets, or weapon hilts. Activate Single Action envision; Frequency once per minute; Effect You channel your life-force into the stone, empowering it temporarily. The stone can detect undead within 60 feet of you, rather than 30 feet, until the end of your turn. Undead hiding or disguising themselves must make an additional Deception or Stealth check to remain disguised or hidden from the activation, and the DC of the check is 23 rather than 20. Activate Two Actions envision, Interact; Frequency one per hour; Effect You focus on the stone as it glows, and your eyes glow with the same tainted light. You detect the auras of evil undead in a 30-foot radius around you and learn each aura's location and strength. This has the effects of a 2nd-level detect alignment spell but only detects evil undead.

---

Contained in a specially enchanted small leather or hide sack, _deteriorating dust_ is a potent caustic agent and a prized item among Rovagug’s more discreet followers.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;     **Effect** You sprinkle the _deteriorating dust_ over an unattended Medium or smaller object. The dust quickly fades to a transparent color and the object immediately begins to rust, melt, or otherwise fall apart. For the listed time, the object takes constant damage; if the object has a Hardness, then the dust gradually reduces the object’s Hardness instead. If the _deteriorating dust_ is still active after the object’s Hardness is reduced to 0, it deals damage to the object as previously described. If the object survives, reduced Hardness returns after the dust’s duration expires, but any damage remains.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Seven Dooms for Sandpoint</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #200: Seven Dooms for Sandpoint](/Sources.aspx?ID=229) pg. 182

**Price** 70 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This 6-inch-long stick of gray-green incense has an unsettling, oily look to it. When burned, a stick of _devil's breath incense_ emits a brimstone-like stink and burns for 10 minutes. Varisian tales claim the stink of this incense closely matches the odor of the breath of the [Sandpoint Devil](/Monsters.aspx?ID=791), although it doesn't come close to the full stink of its flaming exhalations. A creature within 10 feet of a stick of burning _devil's breath incense_ must succeed at a DC 23 Fortitude save or become [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) 1 (sickened 2 on a critical failure), after which they're temporarily immune to the incense for 1 hour.

 While a stick of _devil's breath incense_ is burning, an adjacent creature can lean over the stick to inhale forcefully as an Interact action. Doing so consumes the entire stick immediately and automatically makes the creature sickened 3, but when the creature exhales its next breath, the cloud of smoke they breathe out attempts to carry with it a single curse the creature is afflicted by. The incense has a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) level of 4 and a +12 modifier for the roll. If used to remove the effects of the Sandpoint Devil's Accursed Breath (or similar effects, such as the Cursed Flames that the goblin witch Minargul can create), the _devil's breath incense_ automatically succeeds at removing the curse, regardless of the level of the curse itself.

---

You've bargained with an imp, one of the least powerful devils, for a fragment of infernal luck. 

**Benefit** Once per day, you can roll a saving throw twice and use the higher result. 

**Payment** At the termination of your mortal life, your soul must serve the imp for 100 years. 

**Hidden Condition** The “termination of mortal life” clause is carefully worded to hasten your demise. You can't use the benefit against a [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=40) effect, and if you roll a failure on a saving throw against a death effect, you get a critical failure instead. 

**Termination Clause** If you critically fail a saving throw against a death effect and do not die, the contract becomes unenforceable on its terms and is voided.

Sometimes known as catching powder or simply “the catch,” this silvered powder was devised to slow the pursuit of House Thrune's fiendish servants. The powder is activated by scattering it in an unoccupied adjacent square. If a [devil](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=389) attempts to _[translocate](/Spells.aspx?ID=1724)_ to a destination within 30 feet of this square, the powder attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=3280) the spell with a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=3280) rank of 3 and a counteract modifier of +13. Regardless of the result, the _devil's trap_ is consumed, but if it succeeds at the counteract attempt, the affected devil can't use actions with the [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710) trait for 1 minute.

---

This _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [returning](/Equipment.aspx?ID=301) [trident](/Weapons.aspx?ID=45)_ is made of an ancient black metal that glistens unnaturally and is cold to the touch. The prongs of this trident drip with metallic lake water. Strikes with the _Devil's Trident_ trigger the weaknesses of any creature with a weakness to water.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> Command;   **Trigger** You critically hit a creature;  **Effect** The target must succeed at a DC 25 Fortitude save or become infected with [sewer haze](/Diseases.aspx?ID=11).

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** The trident casts 3rd-level [_quench_](/Spells.aspx?ID=709) with a DC of 25 and a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) modifier of +15. You can Sustain the Spell as normal.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You call upon the corrupted power of the trident to stay a foe. Attempt a Strike. On a hit, the trident casts 3rd-level [_paralyze_](/Spells.aspx?ID=213) on the target (DC 25). If the Strike was a critical hit, the target is [stunned 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36) even if it critically succeeds at the save.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=579" />
<trait label="Focused" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=609" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 288

**Price** 1,250 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn garment

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These vestments are made of panels showing various scenes from the legends of a particular deity. It serves as a religious symbol of that deity, and you gain a +2 item bonus to Religion checks. When you cast [_harm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=146) or [_heal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=148), healing granted to followers of that deity is increased by the rank of the spell. 

**Activate—Domain Devotion** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Gain 1 Focus Point, which you can spend only to cast a cleric domain spell for a domain belonging to the deity the vestments are dedicated to. If you don't spend this point by the end of this turn, it is lost.

**Craft Requirements** You are a cleric who worships the deity tied to the vestments.

</column>

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The next creature you successfully Strike with this weapon is exposed to amnesia venom.

 **Amnesia Venom** ([mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) **Saving Throw** DC 29 Fortitude; **Maximum Duration** 6 rounds; **Stage 1** [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) (1 round); **Stage 2** off-guard and [clumsy 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3) (1 round); **Stage 3** [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=5), off-guard, and clumsy 2 (1 round)

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include a pitcher from a dezullon or similar creature.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Apex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=10" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 603

**Price** 15,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn circlet

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

An elegant, colorful gem cut into a complex geometric pattern is slotted into a narrow metal band that fits around your brow. You gain a +3 item bonus to checks to Recall Knowledge, regardless of the skill. When you invest the diadem, you either increase your Intelligence score by 2 or increase it to 18, whichever would give you a higher score. This gives you additional trained skills and languages, as normal for increasing your Intelligence score. You must select skills and languages the first time you invest the item, and whenever you invest the same _diadem of intellect_, you get the same skills and languages you chose the first time.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You gain the effects of [_hypercognition_](/Spells.aspx?ID=156).

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=564" />
<trait label="Healing" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=623" />

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This thick, red liquid has a pungent—but not unpleasant—smell. You pour the oil onto a weapon when activating it. If the weapon has damaged a creature within the last 10 minutes, the most recent creature damaged by the weapon regains the listed number of Hit Points. The creature is then temporarily immune to _Digly's oil of sympathy_ for 10 minutes.

 The magic relies on the malice behind the attack, so the weapon must have been used against an enemy of the attacker. In other words, someone can't voluntarily take damage from a friend's weapon, then heal from it—a fact that made it very difficult for Sir Kenelm Digly to test the oil during its development.

fields.text: Item 1+ Digly's Oil of Sympathy Rare Consumable Healing Magical Oil Source NPC Core pg. 65 Usage held in 1 hand Bulk L Activate Single Action (manipulate) This thick, red liquid has a pungent—but not unpleasant—smell. You pour the oil onto a weapon when activating it. If the weapon has damaged a creature within the last 10 minutes, the most recent creature damaged by the weapon regains the listed number of Hit Points. The creature is then temporarily immune to Digly's oil of sympathy for 10 minutes. The magic relies on the malice behind the attack, so the weapon must have been used against an enemy of the attacker. In other words, someone can't voluntarily take damage from a friend's weapon, then heal from it—a fact that made it very difficult for Sir Kenelm Digly to test the oil during its development.
